# word owl draft - TOEFL + old registry

# 来源：托福书提供音标/释义/切割/搭配；旧 registry 提供词组和通过污染检查的真例句。
# 托福书整句例句本轮不直接进入成品。

abandon [əˈbændən]
cut:
a/band/on
离开/控制；命令/动作

1. v. 放弃；中止 give up
example: The research team had to abandon the survey when the river flooded the only road.
example_zh: 河水淹没唯一道路后，研究团队不得不放弃这次调查。
phrase: abandon a plan - 放弃计划
phrase: abandon an old system - 放弃旧制度

2. v. 遗弃；抛弃 desert, leave behind
example: Families rarely abandon their homes unless war or drought leaves no safe choice.
example_zh: 除非战争或干旱让人别无安全选择，否则家庭很少会遗弃家园。
phrase: abandoned children - 被遗弃儿童
phrase: abandoned industrial site - 废弃工业场地

abandonment [əˈbændənmənt]
cut:
a/band/on/ment
离开/控制；命令/动作/名词

1. n. 放弃；中止 giving up
phrase: abandonment of treaty obligations - 放弃条约义务

2. n. 遗弃；废弃 desertion
phrase: child abandonment - 遗弃儿童

abbreviate [əˈbriːvieɪt]
cut:
ab/brevi/ate
使；加强/短/动词

1. v. 缩短；节略 shorten
example: Editors often abbreviate long titles so they fit neatly in a catalogue.
example_zh: 编辑常常缩短长标题，使它们能整齐地放进目录。
phrase: abbreviate a title - 缩短标题
phrase: abbreviate a name - 缩写姓名

2. v. 缩写 shorten into initials
example: Scientific writers abbreviate common terms after spelling them out the first time.
example_zh: 科学写作者在第一次完整写出常用术语后，会把它们缩写。
phrase: abbreviate a term - 缩写术语
phrase: abbreviated form - 缩写形式

abide [əˈbaɪd]
cut:
a/bide
加强/停留；等待

1. v. 遵守；遵循 obey, follow
example: Citizens are more likely to abide by rules when authorities explain them clearly.
example_zh: 当当局清楚解释规则时，市民更可能遵守规则。
phrase: abide by rules - 遵守规则
phrase: abide by law - 遵守法律

2. v. 忍受；容忍 tolerate, endure
example: The scientist could not abide careless data because one error might spoil years of work.
example_zh: 这位科学家无法容忍粗心数据，因为一个错误就可能毁掉多年的工作。
phrase: cannot abide noise - 无法忍受噪音
phrase: abide delay - 忍受延迟

3. v. 持续；停留 remain, stay
example: A sense of fear may abide in a community long after the disaster has ended.
example_zh: 灾难结束很久之后，恐惧感仍可能留存在一个社区中。
phrase: abiding respect - 持久尊重
phrase: abiding concern - 持久关切

ability [əˈbɪləti]
cut:
abil/ity
能够；有能力/名词

1. n. 能力；才干 capacity, skill
example: Children develop the ability to compare shapes before they can explain the rule in words.
example_zh: 儿童在能用语言解释规则之前，就已经发展出比较形状的能力。
phrase: cognitive ability - 认知能力
phrase: ability to adapt - 适应能力
phrase: learning ability - 学习能力

2. n. 能够做到的条件；可能性 capability, possibility
example: The new bridge improved the village's ability to reach markets during the rainy season.
example_zh: 新桥提高了这个村庄在雨季抵达市场的能力。
phrase: ability to respond - 应对能力
phrase: technical ability - 技术能力

absolute [ˈæbsəluːt]
cut:

example: The ruler claimed absolute power, but local courts still resisted some orders.

example: Moral absolutes are difficult to apply when two duties conflict.

absolve [əbˈzɑːlv]

ab/solve
离开/松开；解开

1. v. 免除责任；解除义务 release, free
example: A signed form does not absolve the company of responsibility for unsafe equipment.

2. v. 赦免；宣告无罪 forgive, acquit
example: The court did not absolve him until new evidence proved he was elsewhere.
example_zh: 直到新证据证明他当时在别处，法院才宣告他无罪。

ab/sorb
进入；加强/吸收

n. 小瀑布 steep small fall of water

example_zh: 催化剂能加快反应而自身不被消耗，这使工业化学更高效。
phrase: chemical catalyst - 化学催化剂
phrase: catalyst for change - 变革催化剂

cavity [ˈkævəti]
cut:

example_zh: 胸腔保护心脏和肺。

2. n. 洞 pit, crater
example: Rainwater collected in a cavity in the rock.
example_zh: 雨水积在岩石的洞里。

cut:


割让；放弃 abandon

channel [ˈtʃænl]
cut:

phrase: air channel - 气管

chip [tʃɪp]
cut:

example_zh: 一块石头碎片从雕像上脱落。

choir [ˈkwaɪər]
cut:

phrase: gospel choir - 福音合唱团
phrase: choir performance - 合唱团演出

christian []
cut:

chronic []
cut:


adj. 慢性的；长期的 quality, property

example_zh: 流行病会在人群中迅速传播，而慢性状况可能让患者承受数十年负担。

circle []
cut:

citadel [ˈsɪtədəl]
cut:

example_zh: 堡垒可以保护统治者，同时让他们与普通生活隔离。

phrase: ancient citadel - 古代堡垒
phrase: fortified citadel - 加固堡垒

civilian [səˈvɪliən]
cut:
civil/ian
民间的/人；形容词

example: Civilian families were moved away from the fighting.
example_zh: 平民家庭被迁离战斗区域。

2. adj. 民间的 folk

example_zh: 民间工厂开始生产医疗设备。

cut:


n. 蛤 shellfish

example_zh: 蛤感到危险时会闭合贝壳。

cliff [klɪf]
cut:

example_zh: 多年海浪侵蚀底部后，悬崖坍塌了。

clog [klɑːɡ]
cut:

example_zh: 树叶会堵塞排水沟，使街道在大雨中被淹。
phrase: clog a road - 堵塞道路

coax [koʊks]
cut:

example_zh: 护士试图哄害怕的孩子吃药。

coil [kɔɪl]
cut:

example_zh: 一卷铜线放在发电机旁边。

2. v. 盘绕 to wind into rings or spirals

combat [ˈkɑːmbæt]
cut:
com/bat
共同/打，击

example: The city planted trees to combat summer heat.
example_zh: 这座城市种树以对抗夏季高温。

comedy [ˈkɑːmədi]
cut:


n. 喜剧 funny drama
example: Comedy can expose social problems without sounding like a lecture.
example_zh: 喜剧可以揭露社会问题，而不像说教。

commit [kəˈmɪt]
cut:


1. v. 承诺 promise
example: The mayor committed to rebuilding the bridge within a year.
example_zh: 市长承诺一年内重建桥梁。

2. v. 负责 obligate
example: Signing the contract commits the company to regular inspections.
example_zh: 签署合同使公司负责定期检查。

3. v. 犯（错） do, pledge
example: The court found that he had committed fraud.
example_zh: 法院认定他犯了欺诈罪。

compel [kəmˈpel]
cut:
com/pel
共同；加强/驱使

example_zh: 不断上涨的医疗成本可能迫使政府改革养老金和保险体系。

phrase: compel companies to change - 迫使公司改变
phrase: compel action - 迫使行动
phrase: compelled by law - 受法律强制

convoy []
cut:
con/voy
共同；加强/名词；形容词

n./v. 车队；护送 escorted group

phrase: military convoy - 军事车队
phrase: convoy route - 车队路线

coral [ˈkɔːrəl]
cut:
co/ral
共同；一起/形容词

1. n. 珊瑚（虫） reef animal, pink-orange colour
example: A healthy coral reef depends partly on plankton, because tiny organisms support much of the marine food web.
example_zh: 健康珊瑚礁在一定程度上依赖浮游生物，因为微小生物支撑着海洋食物网的大部分。

2. adj. 珊瑚色的，珊瑚红的 reef animal, pink-orange colour
example: The child chose a coral scarf for the summer festival.
example_zh: 孩子为夏季节日选择了一条珊瑚红围巾。

corpse []
cut:


n./v. 尸体 carcass
phrase: human corpse - 人体尸体
phrase: animal corpse - 动物尸体
phrase: corpse decomposition - 尸体分解

cost [kɔːst]
cut:


1. n. 成本，费用，代价 expense
example: The cost of clean water rose after the drought.
example_zh: 干旱后清洁水成本上升。

2. v. 价值为，花费 bloom
example: The repair will cost more than the family can pay.
example_zh: 维修花费将超过这个家庭能支付的金额。

cousin [ˈkʌzn]
cut:


n. 堂（或表）兄弟，堂（或表）姐妹 brother
example: Her cousin helped repair the boat before the fishing season began.
example_zh: 捕鱼季开始前，她的堂亲帮忙修船。

cut:


1. v. （使）破裂 break
example: Heat caused the glass to crack across the middle.
example_zh: 高温使玻璃从中间裂开。

2. n. 裂（缝、纹） split
example: A crack in the wall widened after the earthquake.
example_zh: 地震后，墙上的裂缝变宽了。

cram [kræm]
cut:

example: Students crammed books into every corner of the small room.
example_zh: 学生把书塞满小房间的每个角落。

2. v. 匆忙准备 hurry

example_zh: 他临时抱佛脚准备考试，而不是稳定学习。

crawl [krɔːl]
cut:
c/raw/l
连接音/生疏的/连接音

v. /n. 缓慢（或费力）地行进，爬行 creep
example: Traffic began to crawl after the accident blocked one lane.
example_zh: 事故堵住一条车道后，交通开始缓慢移动。

credit [ˈkredɪt]
cut:


1. n. 荣誉 honour, trust, loan
example: The rescue workers deserve credit for saving the village.
example_zh: 救援人员因拯救村庄而应得荣誉。

2. n. 学分 honour, trust, loan
example: The course gives three credits toward graduation.
example_zh: 这门课为毕业提供三个学分。

3. n. 信用 honour, trust, loan
example: Good credit allowed the family to borrow at a lower rate.
example_zh: 良好信用使这个家庭能以较低利率借款。

4. n. 银行存款 honour, trust, loan, deposit
example: The account showed a small credit after the refund.
example_zh: 退款后，账户显示一小笔存款。

creep [kriːp]
cut:


1. v. 慢慢行进 move slowly
example: Mist crept slowly across the fields at dawn.
example_zh: 黎明时，雾慢慢掠过田野。

2. v. 爬行 crawl
example: The insect crept under the leaf to hide.
example_zh: 昆虫爬到叶子下面躲藏。

crew [kruː]
cut:

example_zh: 全体船员在风暴后修理船只。

2. n. 全体工作人员 working team, staff

criterion [kraɪˈtɪriən]
cut:

example_zh: 与预期结果的大偏差可能迫使研究者重新考虑用于评价的主要标准。

crown [kraʊn]
cut:
crow/n
乌鸦/连接音

1. n. 王冠 royal headpiece

example_zh: 国王的王冠保存在有守卫的房间里。

cruise []
cut:

cut:

example: Cubism breaks objects into shapes seen from several angles.
example_zh: 立体主义把物体拆成从多个角度看到的形状。

cut:

example_zh: 设计良好的课程应体现可靠教学法和认知研究，而不只是列出要考试的话题。

cut:

custom [ˈkʌstəm]
cut:


1. n. ［常pl.］进口税 duties

example_zh: 进口布料的关税使本地商品更便宜。

2. n. 海关 border duty
example: Customs officers inspected the shipment at the port.
example_zh: 海关人员在港口检查货物。

daily []
cut:


每⽇的；⽇常的；每天

damp [dæmp]
cut:
dam/p
水坝/连接音

adj. 潮湿的 moist
example: Damp walls can damage books and make a room smell old.
example_zh: 潮湿墙壁会损坏书籍，并让房间闻起来陈旧。

data [ˈdeɪtə]
cut:

example_zh: 可靠数据帮助医生公平比较治疗方法。

date [deɪt]
cut:


v. 注明…的日期 mark the time of

example_zh: 考古学家用陶器碎片确定该聚落的年代。

dawn [dɔːn]
cut:

example: Fishermen left the harbour at dawn.
example_zh: 渔民在黎明离开港口。

2. n. 开端 outset
example: The invention marked the dawn of modern surgery.

daylight [ˈdeɪlaɪt]
cut:
day/light
白天/光

example: Daylight entered the cave through a narrow opening.
example_zh: 日光通过狭窄开口进入洞穴。

2. n. 白昼 natural light

example_zh: 工人利用每一小时白昼修理屋顶。

3. n. 黎明 dawn
example: They reached the village at daylight after walking all night.
example_zh: 他们走了一整夜，在黎明到达村庄。

deal [diːl]
cut:
deal

1. n. 数量；程度 amount, extent

example_zh: 报告发布前，仍有大量证据需要核查。

2. n. 交易；协议 agreement, transaction
example: The two companies reached a deal after several weeks of careful negotiation.
example_zh: 经过数周谨慎谈判，两家公司达成了一项协议。
phrase: reach a deal - 达成协议

3. v. 处理；应对 handle, manage
example: Local officials had to deal with flooding before schools could reopen.
example_zh: 学校重新开放前，地方官员必须处理洪水问题。
phrase: deal with flooding - 处理洪水问题

4. v. 经营；买卖 trade, do business
example: The shop deals in old maps, scientific instruments, and rare travel books.
example_zh: 这家店经营旧地图、科学仪器和珍稀旅行书籍。
phrase: deal in old maps - 经营旧地图

decade [ˈdekeɪd]
cut:
deca/de
十/向下；离开

n. 十年 ten years
example: The city changed more in one decade than in the previous fifty years.
example_zh: 这座城市在十年中的变化超过此前五十年。
phrase: decade of growth - 增长的十年

decay [dɪˈkeɪ]
cut:


1. v. /n. 腐烂 rot
example: Fruit decays quickly in warm, wet air.
example_zh: 水果在温暖潮湿空气中很快腐烂。

2. v. 衰落 decline
example: The port decayed after trade moved to the railway.
example_zh: 贸易转向铁路后，港口衰落了。

degree [dɪˈɡriː]
cut:

example_zh: 损坏程度因房屋而异。

2. n. 度数 level, angle unit
example: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
example_zh: 水在零摄氏度结冰。

3. n. 学位 level, angle unit
example: She earned a degree in environmental science.
example_zh: 她获得了环境科学学位。

4. n. 等级 grade
example: Different degrees of protection apply to different species.
example_zh: 不同等级保护适用于不同物种。

delay [dɪˈleɪ]
cut:
de/lay
向下；离开/放下

v. /n. 耽搁，延迟 postpone
example: A short delay at the port can affect shops hundreds of kilometres away.
example_zh: 港口的短暂延误会影响数百公里外的商店。
phrase: treatment delay - 治疗延误
phrase: delay a decision - 推迟决定
phrase: long delay - 长时间延误

device [dɪˈvaɪs]
cut:


1. n. 装置，设备 equipment, apparatus
example: A digital device can expand access while creating new forms of dependence.
example_zh: 数字设备可以扩大可及性，同时制造新的依赖形式。

2. n. 手法 technique
example: The writer used repetition as a device to build tension.
example_zh: 作者把重复作为营造紧张感的手法。

devoid [dɪˈvɔɪd]
cut:
de/void
向下；离开/空

adj. 全无的 empty
example: The report was devoid of evidence, so the committee rejected it.
example_zh: 这份报告没有证据，因此委员会拒绝了它。
phrase: devoid of evidence - 缺乏证据
phrase: devoid of emotion - 缺乏情感
phrase: devoid of meaning - 缺乏意义
phrase: devoid of support - 缺乏支持

devote [dɪˈvoʊt]
cut:
de/vote
加强/发誓

1. v. 为…付出（时间、精力等） give fully
example: The team devoted two years to collecting oral histories.
example_zh: 团队为收集口述历史付出了两年时间。

2. v. 献身于 dedicate
example: She devoted herself to improving rural education.
example_zh: 她献身于改善农村教育。

3. v. 作…之用 set aside for purpose
example: The old warehouse was devoted to storing medical supplies.
example_zh: 旧仓库被用作储存医疗用品。

dive [daɪv]
cut:


1. n. /v. 跳水 water
example: The swimmer made a clean dive from the platform.
example_zh: 游泳者从跳台完成了一次利落跳水。

2. n. 潜水 submerge
example: Researchers dived below the reef to examine the damage.
example_zh: 研究者潜入礁石下方检查损害。

divert [daɪˈvɜːrt]
cut:
di/vert
离开/转

1. v. 转移 distract
example: Bike lanes can divert traffic away from crowded roads and improve air quality.
example_zh: 自行车道可以把交通从拥挤道路转移出去，并改善空气质量。

2. v. 使娱乐 amuse, entertain
example: Street music diverted children waiting in the long queue.
example_zh: 街头音乐娱乐了排长队等待的孩子。

doctrine [ˈdɑːktrɪn]
cut:
doc/trine
教/名词

1. n. 教义；教条 teaching, dogma
example: A political doctrine can shape laws long after its original author is gone.
example_zh: 一种政治学说可以在作者离世很久后继续影响法律。
phrase: religious doctrine - 宗教教义

2. n. 学说；原则 theory, principle
example: The doctrine shaped how judges understood property rights.
example_zh: 这套学说影响法官理解财产权的方式。
phrase: economic doctrine - 经济学说

dolphin [ˈdɑːlfɪn]
cut:


n. 海豚 marine mammal
example: A dolphin uses sound to locate fish in cloudy water.
example_zh: 海豚用声音在浑浊水中定位鱼群。

double []
cut:


双重的；复式的
phrase: double structure - 双重结构

downward [ˈdaʊnwərd]
cut:
down/ward
向下的/方向

1. adj. 向下的 moving down
example: The downward slope made the road dangerous in winter.
example_zh: 向下斜坡使道路在冬季很危险。

2. adv. 向下，往下 down
example: The smoke moved downward when cold air entered the tunnel.
example_zh: 冷空气进入隧道时，烟往下移动。

dozen [ˈdʌzn]
cut:


n. 一打，十二个 twelve
example: A dozen families moved after the river changed course.
example_zh: 河流改道后，十二户家庭搬走了。
phrase: dozens of - 许多的

drain [dreɪn]
cut:


1. n. 排水 water
example: The drain carried rainwater away from the street.
example_zh: 排水管把雨水从街道排走。

2. n. 消耗 expenditure
example: The long conflict became a drain on public money.
example_zh: 长期冲突成了公共资金的消耗。

3. v. （使）流走 flow away
example: The fields drained slowly after the storm.
example_zh: 暴风雨后，田地排水很慢。

drill [drɪl]
cut:


1. v. 钻（孔），打眼 bore
example: Workers drilled holes for the bridge foundations.
example_zh: 工人为桥梁地基钻孔。

2. n. 钻（孔） boring tool, practice
example: The dentist used a drill to remove damaged tooth material.
example_zh: 牙医用钻头去除受损牙质。

3. n. 操练 practice
example: A fire drill taught students how to leave the building safely.
example_zh: 消防演练教学生如何安全离开建筑。

drop [drɑːp]
cut:


1. n. 滴 small falling amount

example_zh: 一滴血就足够检测。

2. n. 落下 small falling amount, fall
example: A sharp drop in temperature followed the storm.

2. v. 利用…产生动力 utilisation, use

hatch [hætʃ]
cut:

phrase: hatch eggs - 孵蛋

herd [hɜːrd]
cut:

example_zh: 一群水牛缓慢走向河流。

heritage [ˈherɪtɪdʒ]
cut:

example_zh: 旅游业应保护文化遗产，而不是把它变成廉价娱乐。

2. n. 传统 tradition

example_zh: 保护文化遗产可以强化身份认同并支持旅游业。

holy []
cut:


神圣的；圣洁的

honest [ˈɑːnɪst]
cut:


1. adj. 诚实的 truthful, sincere

example_zh: 诚实证人承认自己不记得的内容。

2. adj. 正直的 upright

example_zh: 正直官员拒绝承包商的礼物。

3. adj. 老实的 truthful, sincere
example: The old farmer preferred honest work to easy profit.
example_zh: 这位老农更喜欢老实劳动，而不是轻松获利。

horn [hɔːrn]
cut:


1. n. （牛、羊、鹿等的）角 angle

example_zh: 山羊的角从头部向后弯曲。

2. n. 号角，喇叭 speaker, trumpet
example: The horn sounded when the ship left the harbour.
example_zh: 船离港时，号角响起。

hover [ˈhʌvər]
cut:


v. 徘徊 wander
example: The helicopter hovered above the roof before lowering the rope.
example_zh: 直升机在屋顶上方盘旋，然后放下绳索。

huddle [ˈhʌdl]
cut:


v. 挤在一起 crowd together

example_zh: 当危险让孤立变得不可能时，人们可能会抱团。
phrase: penguin huddle - 企鹅抱团
phrase: huddle for warmth - 抱团取暖
phrase: rotating huddle - 轮换抱团
phrase: huddle together - 挤在一起

hurl [hɜːrl]
cut:
hurl

v. 猛投，用力投掷 fling
example: Strong waves hurled stones against the sea wall.
example_zh: 强浪把石块猛撞向海堤。

husk [hʌsk]
cut:


1. n. （果类或谷物的）外壳 grain
example: The husk protected the grain until harvest.
example_zh: 外壳保护谷粒直到收获。

2. n. 皮 shell, outer covering

example_zh: 干皮躺在种子旁边。

3. v. 剥…的壳 peel
example: Workers husked corn before drying it.
example_zh: 工人在晾干玉米前剥去外壳。

4. v. 削皮 peel
example: She husked the fruit with a small knife.
example_zh: 她用小刀削去水果皮。

infest [ɪnˈfest]
cut:
infest

1. v. 骚扰 harassment

example_zh: 洪水后，蚊子骚扰营地。

2. v. 大批滋生 invade in numbers

example_zh: 老鼠在储存谷物的仓库里大批滋生。

innate [ɪˈneɪt]
cut:
in/nat/e
向内/出生的/e

adj. 天生的 inborn

example_zh: 有些恐惧似乎是天生的，另一些则来自经验学习。

insect [ˈɪnsekt]

in/sect
进入；切入/切

example_zh: 昆虫寻找食物时可以给花授粉。

phrase: small insect - 小昆虫
phrase: disease-carrying insect - 携病昆虫

insist [ɪnˈsɪst]
cut:
in/sist
里面/站

example_zh: 医生坚持认为洪水后清洁水源至关重要。
phrase: insist on - 坚持

intact [ɪnˈtækt]
cut:
in/tact
不/接触

example_zh: 尽管发生地震，这只古代花瓶仍完好无损。

item [ˈaɪtəm]
cut:

example_zh: 合同第一条规定付款日期。

2. n. 项目 single thing in a list
example: Each item on the list must be checked before departure.
example_zh: 出发前必须检查清单上的每个项目。

jolt [dʒoʊlt]
cut:

example_zh: 这条消息震惊了原本期待市场平静的投资者。

2. n. 震动 shake
example: A sudden jolt shook the train as it stopped.
example_zh: 火车停下时，一阵突然震动摇晃了车厢。

juice [dʒuːs]
cut:


n. 汁，液 fruit liquid
example: Fruit juice spoiled quickly because the bottle was not sealed.
example_zh: 果汁很快变质，因为瓶子没有密封。

justice [ˈdʒʌstɪs]
cut:

example: The justice listened to arguments from both lawyers.
example_zh: 法官听取了双方律师的论点。

2. n. 公正 equity
example: Justice requires equal treatment before the law.
example_zh: 公正要求法律面前平等对待。

3. n. 司法 judicial
example: The justice system was slow but finally corrected the error.
example_zh: 司法系统虽慢，但最终纠正了错误。

juvenile [ˈdʒuːvənl]
cut:
juven/ile
年轻/…的

1. n. 少年 young person or animal

example_zh: 法院因他未满十八岁而把他视为少年。

example_zh: 该物种幼体的斑纹比成体更浅。

3. adj. 少年的 young person or animal
example: Juvenile crime fell after youth centres opened.
example_zh: 青年中心开放后，少年犯罪下降。

4. adj. 未成熟的 young person or animal, immature
example: The review called the insult juvenile and unhelpful.
example_zh: 评论称这种侮辱未成熟且无益。

label [ˈleɪbl]
cut:


1. n. 标签 tag
example: The label listed the medicine's ingredients.
example_zh: 标签列出了药品成分。

2. v. 标记 mark
example: Researchers labelled each sample before freezing it.
example_zh: 研究者在冷冻前标记每个样本。

lace [leɪs]
cut:

example_zh: 这条裙子饰有白色蕾丝。

2. n. 缎带 decorative fabric, ribbon

example_zh: 一条红缎带把包裹系紧。

lash [læʃ]
cut:
l/ash
连接音/灰

example_zh: 风暴前，水手把箱子系牢在甲板上。

example_zh: 雨整夜猛烈打击窗户。

league [liːɡ]
cut:

example_zh: 几个城镇组成联盟，以保护沿河贸易。

leap [liːp]
cut:

example_zh: 鹿跳过狭窄溪流。

2. n. 跳跃 jump
example: The athlete's leap broke the school record.
example_zh: 这名运动员的跳跃打破了校纪录。

example: The discovery caused a leap in medical understanding.
example_zh: 这一发现带来了医学理解的骤变。

lens [lenz]

example_zh: 布满灰尘的镜头使照片不清晰。

example: His glasses needed a stronger lens for reading.

lesson []
cut:


一节课；一课时；经验；教训 experience

lettuce [ˈletɪs]

level [ˈlevl]

example_zh: 三天降雨后，水位上升。

example_zh: 这个级别的学生能阅读短科学文本。

3. adj. 水平的 horizontal

4. v. 夷平，使平坦 height, stage, flatten
example: The earthquake levelled several old houses.

liber/ty
自由/性质；状态

phrase: civil liberty - 公民自由

library/ian
librar(y)（图书馆）/人；形容词

n. 图书管理员 management

example_zh: 图书管理员帮助学生为历史项目寻找资料。

like []
cut:


像v.喜欢n.喜好

list [lɪst]
cut:

example_zh: 表中包括工具、食物和急救药品。

2. v. 把…编列成表，列入表内 written series

literature [ˈlɪtrətʃər]
cut:

example_zh: 文献综述显示一项研究进入既有争论的位置。

2. n. 文学作品 literary

example_zh: 现代文学作品常探索记忆与身份。

example_zh: 医学文献描述了几个类似病例。

cut:
live/stock
活/东西

example_zh: 当混合农场既要生产食物又要维持土壤质量时，农民可能把作物栽培和牲畜管理结合起来。

cut:

example_zh: 蜥蜴捕食昆虫前在岩石上晒暖身体。

load [loʊd]
cut:

example_zh: 高工资吸引工人来到矿镇。

2. n. 诱惑力 attraction, bait

cut:
magn/itude
大/状态

male [meɪl]
cut:

example_zh: 男性工人曾因同样工作获得更高工资。

2. n. 男子 masculine, animal sex, man

example_zh: 调查统计了村里每位成年男子。

3. n. 雄性动物 sexually masculine creature
example: The male guards the eggs until they hatch.
example_zh: 雄性动物守护卵直到孵化。

cut:
mar/ble
三月/能够；形容词

example: The palace floor was made of white marble.
example_zh: 宫殿地板由白色大理石制成。

2. n. 雕塑品 sculpture
example: A marble of the queen stood in the courtyard.
example_zh: 女王雕塑品立在庭院里。

march [mɑːrtʃ]
cut:

example: The band played a march during the parade.
example_zh: 乐队在游行中演奏进行曲。

2. v. 前进，行进 walk in order, parade music
example: Workers marched toward the capital to demand fair wages.
example_zh: 工人向首都行进，要求公平工资。

maritime [ˈmærɪtaɪm]
cut:

example: Maritime winds kept the island climate mild.
example_zh: 海风使岛屿气候温和。

2. adj. 航海的 sea-related
example: Maritime law governs accidents between ships.
example_zh: 航海法管理船舶之间的事故。

match [mætʃ]
cut:

example: The football match ended without a goal.
example_zh: 这场足球比赛以零进球结束。

2. n. 对手 opponent
example: The champion finally met a serious match.
example_zh: 冠军终于遇到强劲对手。

3. v. 和…相配 suit
example: The paint should match the colour of the old wall.
example_zh: 油漆应与旧墙颜色相配。

mate [meɪt]
cut:

example_zh: 这种鸟每年春天回到同一配偶身边。

2. v. 配对 partner, pair

3. v. 交配 copulate
example: Some insects mate only once in their lives.
example_zh: 有些昆虫一生只交配一次。

matrix []
cut:

example_zh: 当许多数值之间的关系必须被组织时，数学定理可以用矩阵表示。

cut:

example: Mature fruit falls easily from the tree.
example_zh: 成熟水果很容易从树上落下。

2. adj. 深思熟虑的 deliberate

example_zh: 深思熟虑的决定会考虑长期后果。

example: The forest will mature after decades of protection.
example_zh: 经过数十年保护，森林会成熟起来。

maximum [ˈmæksɪməm]
cut:

medal [ˈmedl]

example: A scientific mind tests ideas against evidence.

example: The pump drew water from the deep well.
example_zh: 泵从深井中抽水。

2. v. （用泵）抽 liquid-moving machine
example: Workers pumped floodwater out of the basement.
example_zh: 工人用泵把洪水从地下室抽出。

pure [pjʊr]
cut:
pur/e
纯净/e

1. adj. 纯净的；洁净的 clean, unmixed
example: Pure water is useful in experiments because it reduces unwanted chemical interference.
example_zh: 纯净水在实验中很有用，因为它能减少不必要的化学干扰。
phrase: pure water - 纯净水
phrase: pure oxygen - 纯氧

2. adj. 完全的；纯粹的 absolute
example: The story was pure invention, not historical fact.
example_zh: 这个故事完全是虚构，不是历史事实。
phrase: pure chance - 纯属偶然

purpose []
cut:


目的；意图；用途；效果 intention

puzzle [ˈpʌzl]
cut:


1. n. 难题，谜 ，迷惑 problem, confuse
example: The missing document became a puzzle for investigators.
example_zh: 丢失文件成了调查人员的难题。

2. v. （使）迷惑 problem, confuse
example: The strange signal puzzled the radio engineers.
example_zh: 奇怪信号使无线电工程师迷惑。

3. v. （使）为难 problem, confuse
example: The math problem puzzled even the strongest students.
example_zh: 这道数学题甚至让最强的学生为难。

quarry [ˈkwɔːri]
cut:


1. n. 石矿 stone, rock
example: Stone from the quarry was used to build the bridge.
example_zh: 石矿中的石头被用来建桥。

2. n. 被追求的人或事物 prey
example: The detective finally found his quarry in a border town.
example_zh: 侦探最终在边境小镇找到了追寻对象。

questionnaire [ˌkwestʃəˈner]
cut:


n. 问卷，调查表 investigation
example: The questionnaire asked residents about transport, safety, and housing.
example_zh: 问卷询问居民关于交通、安全和住房的问题。

rainbow [ˈreɪnboʊ]
cut:


n. 虹 coloured arc
example: A rainbow appeared after sunlight passed through the rain.
example_zh: 阳光穿过雨水后出现了彩虹。

range [reɪndʒ]
cut:


1. n. 范围 extent
example: The course covers a wide range of environmental issues.
example_zh: 这门课涵盖广泛环境问题。

2. n. 山脉 mountain
example: A snow-covered range rose beyond the valley.
example_zh: 一列雪山在山谷之外升起。

3. v. （在某范围内）变动 vary, extend
example: Temperatures range from freezing nights to hot afternoons.
example_zh: 温度在寒冷夜晚和炎热下午之间变动。

rank [ræ k]
cut:


1. n. 等级 grade
example: Military rank determined where each officer stood.
example_zh: 军衔决定每位军官所站位置。

2. n. 头衔 title
example: The title gave him rank but little real power.
example_zh: 这个头衔给了他地位，但几乎没有实权。

3. v. 属于某等级，归类 class
example: The school ranks among the best in the region.
example_zh: 这所学校属于该地区最好的学校之一。

rare [rer]
cut:


1. adj. 稀有的，罕见的 infrequent
example: Rare birds nest in the wetland each spring.
example_zh: 罕见鸟类每年春天在湿地筑巢。

2. adj. （肉类）半熟的 underdone
example: The steak was served rare, with a red centre.
example_zh: 牛排半熟上桌，中间呈红色。

ratio [ˈreɪʃioʊ]
cut:


n. 比，比率 proportion
example: The ratio of teachers to students affects how much feedback each learner receives.
example_zh: 教师与学生的比例会影响每个学习者获得多少反馈。
phrase: high ratio - 高比例
phrase: student-teacher ratio - 师生比
phrase: debt ratio - 债务比率

reach [riːtʃ]
cut:


1. v. 抵达 ，达到 arrive at, stretch to
example: The hikers reached the village before dark.
example_zh: 徒步者在天黑前抵达村庄。

2. v. 伸手，够到，触到 arrive at, stretch to
example: She reached for the rope but could not catch it.
example_zh: 她伸手去够绳子，但没抓住。

3. n. 能达到的范围 arrive at, stretch to
example: The station lies within reach of several mountain towns.
example_zh: 这个车站位于几个山镇能到达的范围内。

realm [relm]
cut:
real/m
真正的/连接音

1. n. 领域 region
example: The question belongs to the realm of public health.
example_zh: 这个问题属于公共卫生领域。

2. n. 王国 kingdom
example: The old map showed the borders of a vanished realm.
example_zh: 旧地图显示了一个消失王国的边界。

recall [rɪˈkɔːl]
cut:


1. v. 回忆（起），回想起 recollect
example: She recalled the smell of the sea from childhood.
example_zh: 她回忆起童年时海的气味。

2. n. 记忆 memory
example: His recall of names was excellent even in old age.
example_zh: 即使年老，他对姓名的记忆也很好。

recent []
cut:


最近的；最新的

recipe [ˈresəpi]
cut:


1. n. 食谱 cookbook
example: The recipe used beans, rice, and dried herbs.
example_zh: 这份食谱使用豆子、米和干草药。

2. n. 方法 method
example: Ignoring safety rules is a recipe for disaster.
example_zh: 忽视安全规则是导致灾难的方法。

regime []
cut:


n. 政权；制度；管理体系 management
example: A weak regime can survive criticism if no convincing rebuttal shows why its rules fail in practice.
example_zh: 薄弱制度若没有有力反驳说明其规则为何在实践中失败，仍可能经受住批评。
phrase: political regime - 政治体制
phrase: regulatory regime - 监管制度
phrase: authoritarian regime - 威权政权
phrase: regime change - 政权更迭

relief [rɪˈliːf]
cut:


1. n. 浮雕 ease, raised sculpture
example: The temple wall showed a relief of farmers harvesting grain.
example_zh: 寺庙墙上有农民收割谷物的浮雕。

2. n. 缓解 ease, raised sculpture
example: Rain brought relief to villages suffering from drought.
example_zh: 降雨给遭受干旱的村庄带来缓解。

remain []
cut:


徘徊；持续存在 persistent, lasting
phrase: remain for years - 持续多年

remind [rɪˈmaɪnd]
cut:


1. v. 提醒 inform
example: The sign reminds visitors to close the gate.
example_zh: 标牌提醒游客关门。

2. v. 使想起 bring to mind
example: The old song reminded her of her grandmother.
example_zh: 这首老歌使她想起祖母。

repel [rɪˈpel]
cut:
re/pel
反/推

1. v. 驱除 drive away
example: The smell of smoke repelled insects from the hut.
example_zh: 烟味驱除了小屋里的昆虫。

2. v. 排斥 exclude
example: Like charges repel each other in physics.
example_zh: 在物理学中，同种电荷相互排斥。

repent []
cut:


后悔；忏悔

report [rɪˈpɔːrt]
cut:


1. n. 报告，汇报 account, tell officially
example: The report described damage to roads and bridges.
example_zh: 报告描述了道路和桥梁的损坏。

2. n. 传说 traditional, legendary
example: There was a report that gold had been found upriver.
example_zh: 有传说称上游发现了黄金。

3. n. 传阅 account, tell officially, circulation
example: The report circulated among officials before publication.
example_zh: 这份传阅材料在发表前在官员之间流转。

4. v. 报告，汇报，报到 account, tell officially
example: Doctors reported three new cases in the village.
example_zh: 医生报告村里新增三例病例。

rescue [ˈreskjuː]
cut:


v. /n. 营救，搭救 save
example: Volunteers helped rescue families trapped by the flood.
example_zh: 志愿者帮助营救被洪水困住的家庭。

resin [ˈrezn]
cut:


n. 树脂 sticky plant substance
example: Tree resin can harden and preserve insects for millions of years.
example_zh: 树脂会硬化，并把昆虫保存数百万年。

resort [rɪˈzɔːrt]
cut:


1. n. 度假胜地 holiday place, turn to
example: The mountain resort attracts visitors in both summer and winter.
example_zh: 这座山区度假胜地夏冬都吸引游客。

2. n. 求助 holiday place, turn to
example: The family used borrowing as a last resort.
example_zh: 这家人把借款作为最后求助手段。

retort []
cut:


（愤怒或⻛趣地）反驳；回嘴；反驳；回嘴 contradiction

revere [rɪˈvɪr]
cut:


v. 尊敬，敬畏 respect
example: Many communities revere elders who preserve local memory.
example_zh: 许多社区尊敬保存地方记忆的长者。

review [rɪˈvjuː]
cut:
re/view
回/看

1. v. 审查 examine again
example: Experts reviewed the bridge design before construction began.
example_zh: 施工开始前，专家审查了桥梁设计。

2. v. 复习 examine again
example: Students reviewed old vocabulary before the test.
example_zh: 学生在考试前复习旧词汇。

3. n. 复习 examine again
example: A short review helped the class remember the main ideas.
example_zh: 简短复习帮助全班记住主要观点。

4. n. 评论 comment
example: The newspaper published a review of the new museum.
example_zh: 报纸发表了对新博物馆的评论。

rhyme [raɪm]
cut:


1. n. 韵，押韵 rhythm
example: The poem uses rhyme to make each line easier to remember.
example_zh: 这首诗使用押韵让每一行更容易记住。

2. v. 押韵 matching sound
example: In English, 'light' can rhyme with 'night'.
example_zh: 英语中，light 可以和 night 押韵。

rigid [ˈrɪdʒɪd]
cut:


1. adj. 严格的 strict
example: Rigid rules left teachers no room to help unusual cases.
example_zh: 严格规则让教师没有空间帮助特殊情况。

2. adj. 刚硬的，不易弯曲的 stiff
example: A rigid metal frame kept the instrument steady.
example_zh: 刚硬金属框架使仪器保持稳定。

rite [raɪt]
cut:


n. （宗教的）仪式 ritual
example: The rite marked the child's entrance into adult society.
example_zh: 这一仪式标志着孩子进入成人社会。

rough [rʌf]
cut:


1. adj. 粗糙不平的 coarse
example: The rough road damaged the wheels of the cart.
example_zh: 粗糙不平的道路损坏了车轮。

2. adj. 粗暴的 tough
example: Rough treatment made the frightened child stop speaking.
example_zh: 粗暴对待让受惊孩子停止说话。

3. adj. 艰难的 uneven, difficult
example: The first winter in the new settlement was rough.
example_zh: 新定居点的第一个冬天很艰难。

4. n. （高尔夫球场的）深草区 uneven, difficult
example: The ball disappeared into the rough beside the fairway.
example_zh: 球消失在球道旁的深草区。

routine [ruːˈtiːn]
cut:


1. n. 惯例，常规 convention
example: Daily routine helped the children feel safe after the move.
example_zh: 搬家后，日常惯例帮助孩子感到安全。

2. adj. 例行的 regular pattern
example: Routine inspections found the crack before the bridge failed.
example_zh: 例行检查在桥梁失效前发现了裂缝。

ruin [ˈruːɪn]
cut:
ruin

1. v. 破坏，毁灭 destroy
example: Repeated floods ruined the lower rooms of the house.
example_zh: 反复洪水毁坏了房子的下层房间。

2. n. [常pl.] 废墟，遗迹 relic
example: Tourists walked among the ruins of the old fort.
example_zh: 游客在旧堡垒遗迹中行走。

rupture [ˈrʌptʃər]
cut:
rupt/ure
断/结果；名词

v. （使）破裂 burst
example: A sudden pressure change can rupture a weak pipe.
example_zh: 压力突然变化会使脆弱管道破裂。
phrase: social rupture - 社会断裂
phrase: rupture a pipe - 弄破管道
phrase: rupture a pattern - 打破模式
phrase: rupture a relationship - 破裂关系

rural [ˈrʊrəl]
cut:
rur/al
乡村/…的

1. adj. 乡村的，农村的 country
example: Rural schools often need better transport and internet access.
example_zh: 农村学校常需要更好的交通和网络。

2. adj. 田园的 field
example: The painting shows a quiet rural landscape after harvest.
example_zh: 这幅画展示了收获后的宁静田园景色。

salmon [ˈsæmən]
cut:


n. 鲑鱼，大马哈鱼 migrating fish
example: Salmon return upstream to reproduce after years in the ocean.
example_zh: 鲑鱼在海洋中生活多年后逆流返回繁殖。

salon [səˈlɑːn]
cut:


n. （营业性的）厅，院，室，店 quality, property
example: The salon became a meeting place for artists and political writers.
example_zh: 这间沙龙成了艺术家和政治作家的聚会地点。
phrase: hair salon - 美发厅

saturn [ˈsætɜːrn]
cut:


n. 土星 soil, earth
example: Saturn is known for its bright rings and many moons.
example_zh: 土星以明亮的环和众多卫星闻名。

save [seɪv]
cut:


1. v. 拯救 rescue
example: Quick action saved the village from the spreading fire.
example_zh: 迅速行动拯救了村庄，使其免遭蔓延火势。

2. v. 保存 store
example: The archive saves copies of every local newspaper.
example_zh: 档案馆保存每份地方报纸的副本。

3. v. 节省 economize
example: Insulation saves energy during cold winters.
example_zh: 隔热材料在寒冷冬季节省能源。

4. prep. 除…之外 except
example: Everyone save the night guard had left the building.
example_zh: 除夜班警卫之外，所有人都离开了建筑。

scan [skæn]
cut:


1. v. 细察 examine, scrutinize
example: The doctor scanned the report for signs of infection.
example_zh: 医生细察报告，寻找感染迹象。

2. v. 扫描 look over, image electronically
example: The machine scanned each page into a digital file.
example_zh: 机器把每一页扫描成数字文件。

scar [skɑːr]
cut:
s/car
连接音/汽车

1. n. 疤痕 seam
example: A long scar remained on his arm after the accident.
example_zh: 事故后，他手臂上留下了一道长疤痕。

2. v. （给…）留下伤痕 blemish
example: The war scarred the city for generations.
example_zh: 战争给这座城市留下了数代人的伤痕。

scarf [skɑːrf]
cut:


n. 围巾，披巾 shawl
example: A wool scarf protected her face from the cold wind.
example_zh: 羊毛围巾保护她的脸免受冷风侵袭。

scene [siːn]
cut:


1. n. 地点，现场 location, spot
example: Police arrived at the scene shortly after the crash.
example_zh: 撞车后不久，警方到达现场。

2. n. 景色 setting, spectacle
example: The lake scene attracted painters every summer.
example_zh: 湖边景色每年夏天吸引画家。

scent [sent]
cut:


1. n. 香气 odor, fragrance
example: The scent of pine filled the mountain cabin.
example_zh: 松香充满了山间小屋。

2. n. 气味 smell
example: Dogs followed the scent across the wet field.
example_zh: 狗沿着气味穿过湿地。

science []
cut:
sci/ence
知道；知识/名词

n. 科学 field of study
example: Science advances when evidence is shared and tested openly.
example_zh: 证据被公开分享和检验时，科学就会进步。
phrase: social science - 社会科学
phrase: natural science - 自然科学

scorch [skɔːrtʃ]
cut:


v. 烤焦 burn, sear
example: The fire scorched the lower branches but did not kill the tree.
example_zh: 火烤焦了低处树枝，但没有烧死这棵树。

seashore [ˈsiːʃɔːr]
cut:


n. 海岸，海滨 coast, beach, shore
example: Children collected shells along the seashore after the tide went out.
example_zh: 退潮后，孩子们沿海岸捡贝壳。

shallow [ˈʃæloʊ]
cut:


adj. 浅的 superficial
example: Shallow water warms quickly in spring.
example_zh: 浅水在春季升温很快。
phrase: shallow explanation - 浅层解释
phrase: shallow water - 浅水
phrase: shallow argument - 肤浅论证
phrase: shallow understanding - 浅层理解

shape [ʃeɪp]
cut:


1. n. 形状. 外形 form
example: The island has the shape of a narrow crescent.
example_zh: 这座岛呈狭长新月形。

2. n. 情况，状态 condition
example: The economy was in poor shape after the conflict.
example_zh: 冲突后，经济状况很差。

3. n. 种类 kind, type
example: Clouds of many shapes moved across the sky.
example_zh: 各种形状的云掠过天空。

4. v. 成型，塑造 form
example: Early experiences can shape a child's confidence.
example_zh: 早期经历会塑造孩子的信心。

sheer [ʃɪr]
cut:


1. adj. 陡峭的 steep
example: A sheer cliff rose behind the village.
example_zh: 村庄后方升起一面陡峭悬崖。

2. adj. 绝对的 absolute
example: The plan failed through sheer lack of preparation.
example_zh: 这个计划完全因准备不足而失败。

shield [ʃiːld]
cut:


1. n. 防护物 defense
example: A glass shield protected workers from flying fragments.
example_zh: 玻璃防护物保护工人免受飞散碎片伤害。

2. n. 盾 protective cover
example: The warrior carried a round wooden shield.
example_zh: 战士携带一面圆木盾。

3. v. 保护 protect, defend
example: Trees shielded the house from winter winds.
example_zh: 树木保护房屋免受冬风侵袭。

shore [ʃɔːr]
cut:


n. 海滨，岸 coast, beach
example: The boat stayed close to shore during the storm.
example_zh: 风暴期间，小船靠近岸边行驶。

shrimp [ʃrɪmp]
cut:


n. 小虾 small shellfish
example: Shrimp farms can damage wetlands if waste is not controlled.
example_zh: 如果废弃物不受控制，养虾场会破坏湿地。

shrink [ʃrɪ k]
cut:


v. 收缩，缩小 dwindle
example: The lake began to shrink after several dry years.
example_zh: 连续几年干旱后，湖泊开始缩小。

shrivel [ˈʃrɪvl]
cut:


v. （使）枯萎 dry and shrink
example: Leaves shrivel when a plant loses too much water.
example_zh: 植物失水过多时，叶子会枯萎。

shrub [ʃrʌb]
cut:


n. 灌木（丛） low woody plant
example: A dense shrub can provide shelter for small birds.
example_zh: 茂密灌木可以为小鸟提供庇护。

sketch [sketʃ]
cut:


1. n. 草稿 draft
example: The engineer made a sketch of the bridge before drawing details.
example_zh: 工程师先画桥梁草稿，再画细节。

2. n. 草图 rough drawing
example: The sketch showed where each room would be placed.
example_zh: 草图显示每个房间的位置。

3. n. 素描 rough drawing
example: A charcoal sketch of the old market hung on the wall.
example_zh: 一幅旧市场木炭素描挂在墙上。

4. v. 给…速写 draw
example: The artist sketched the harbour while boats returned.
example_zh: 船只返港时，艺术家给港口速写。

skull [skʌl]
cut:


1. n. 颅骨 head bone
example: The skull protected the brain inside the fossil.
example_zh: 颅骨保护着化石内部的大脑。

2. n. 头脑 mind
example: He used his skull and solved the problem quietly.
example_zh: 他动了头脑，安静地解决了问题。

slice [slaɪs]
cut:


1. v. 切（片） thin piece, cut thin
example: The cook sliced the bread before serving soup.
example_zh: 厨师在上汤前把面包切片。

2. n. 薄片 flake
example: A thin slice of rock was examined under the microscope.
example_zh: 一片薄岩石在显微镜下被检查。

3. n. 片断 segment
example: The story shows only a slice of life in the capital.
example_zh: 这个故事只展示了首都生活的一个片段。

slide [slaɪd]
cut:
s/lid/e
连接音/盖子/e

1. v. 滑动 glide, slip
example: Mud slid down the hill after heavy rain.
example_zh: 大雨后，泥土从山坡滑下。

2. n. 滑动 slippage
example: The slide of loose stones blocked the path.
example_zh: 松石滑落堵住了小路。

3. n. 幻灯片 slip, visual page
example: The lecturer showed a slide of the ancient temple.
example_zh: 讲师展示了一张古庙幻灯片。

slip [slɪp]
cut:
s/lip
连接音/嘴唇

1. v. 滑（过、落） slide
example: The child slipped on the wet floor.
example_zh: 孩子在湿地板上滑倒。

2. n. （木、纸）片 paper
example: She wrote the address on a small slip of paper.
example_zh: 她把地址写在一小片纸上。

3. n. 滑倒 slide, small mistake

障碍/获得

1. n. 廉价货 cheap deal, negotiate
example: The used bicycle was a bargain at that price.
example_zh: 以那个价格买这辆二手自行车很划算。

2. n. 交易 transaction
example: The bargain gave farmers a fairer price for grain.
example_zh: 这笔交易给农民更公平的谷物价格。

3. n. 契约，合同 cheap deal, negotiate, contract
example: The bargain between the two towns fixed water use.
example_zh: 两个城镇之间的契约确定了用水方式。

4. v. 议价 cheap deal, negotiate
example: Workers bargained for safer conditions.
example_zh: 工人为更安全条件议价。

barge [bɑːrdʒ]
cut:


1. n. 驳船 flat boat
example: A barge carried coal along the canal.
example_zh: 一艘驳船沿运河运煤。

2. n. 游艇 flat boat
example: Tourists rented a small barge for the river festival.
example_zh: 游客为河流节租了一艘小游艇。

bark [bɑːrk]
cut:


n. 树皮 tree outer layer
example: Tree bark protects the trunk from insects and heat.
example_zh: 树皮保护树干免受昆虫和高温侵害。

barn [bɑːrn]
cut:


1. n. 谷仓 farm storage building
example: The harvest was stored in a red barn.
example_zh: 收成储存在红色谷仓里。

2. n. 牲口棚 farm storage building
example: The old barn sheltered cattle during winter storms.
example_zh: 旧牲口棚在冬季风暴中庇护牛群。

bead [biːd]
cut:


n. 珠子，水珠 water
example: A bead of water rolled down the glass.
example_zh: 一滴水珠沿玻璃滚下。

beaver [ˈbiːvər]
cut:


n. 海狸 dam-building rodent
example: A beaver builds dams that change the flow of streams.
example_zh: 海狸筑坝，改变溪流流向。
phrase: beaver dam - 河狸坝
phrase: beaver pond - 河狸池塘
phrase: beaver changes rivers - 河狸改变河流

behavior [bɪˈheɪvjər]
cut:


n. 举止，行为 conduct, manner
example: Animal behavior changes when food becomes scarce.
example_zh: 食物变得稀少时，动物行为会改变。

belie [bɪˈlaɪ]
cut:
be/lie
使；加强/谎言

1. v. 给人错觉 misrepresent
example: The calm surface belied the dangerous current below.
example_zh: 平静水面给人错觉，掩盖了下方危险水流。

2. v. 掩饰 disguise
example: His smile belied his disappointment.
example_zh: 他的微笑掩饰了失望。

bellows [ˈbeloʊz]
cut:


n. 风箱 air-blowing tool
example: The blacksmith used bellows to make the fire hotter.
example_zh: 铁匠用风箱让火更旺。

benign [bɪˈnaɪn]
cut:
ben/ign
好/形容词后缀

1. adj. （病）良性的 innocuous
example: The doctor said the tumour was benign.
example_zh: 医生说肿瘤是良性的。

2. adj. 和蔼的 kind
example: The old teacher had a benign manner with nervous children.
example_zh: 老教师对紧张孩子态度和蔼。

besides [bɪˈsaɪdz]
cut:


1. prep. 除…之外 except, save
example: Besides medicine, the clinic needed blankets and clean water.
example_zh: 除药品之外，诊所还需要毯子和清洁水。

2. adv. 而且，还有 also, in addition
example: The road was dangerous; besides, it was already dark.
example_zh: 道路很危险，而且天已经黑了。

besiege [bɪˈsiːdʒ]
cut:
be/siege
使；加强/包围

v. 包围 surround
example: A city under siege may suffer hunger, disease, and social collapse.
example_zh: 被围攻的城市可能遭受饥饿、疾病和社会崩溃。
phrase: besiege a city - 围攻城市
phrase: be besieged by problems - 被问题包围
phrase: besieged city - 被围困城市

bet [bet]
cut:


n. /v. 打赌 wager
example: The farmer made a risky bet on early rain.
example_zh: 农民把希望押在早雨上，冒了风险。
phrase: I bet that… - 我敢肯定
phrase: You bet - 的确，当然

bias [ˈbaɪəs]
cut:
bi/as
两/朝向；加强

n. 偏见 prejudice
example: Biased reporting can distort public views on crime, immigration, and government spending.
example_zh: 有偏见的报道可能扭曲公众对犯罪、移民和政府支出的看法。
phrase: media bias - 媒体偏见
phrase: biased judgement - 有偏见判断
phrase: biased reporting - 有偏见报道
phrase: biased sampling method - 有偏抽样方法

bicameral [ˌbaɪˈkæmərəl]
cut:


adj. 两院制的，有两个议院的 two-chambered
example: A bicameral parliament has two separate chambers.
example_zh: 两院制议会有两个独立议院。

biochemical [ˌbaɪoʊˈkemɪkl]
cut:


adj. 生物化学的 biological
example: Biochemical reactions allow cells to release energy from food.
example_zh: 生物化学反应让细胞从食物中释放能量。
phrase: biochemical marker of disease - 疾病生化标志物
phrase: biochemical pathway analysis - 生化通路分析

biography [baɪˈɑːɡrəfi]
cut:
bio/graph/y
生命/写/名词；形容词

n. 传记 life story
example: The biography explains how early poverty shaped the scientist's work.
example_zh: 这本传记解释了早年贫困如何塑造这位科学家的工作。
phrase: written biography - 书面传记
phrase: scientific biography - 科学家传记

bland [blænd]
cut:


adj. 无味的 mild, flavourless
example: The bland food was safe for patients with stomach problems.
example_zh: 清淡食物适合胃部有问题的病人。

bleach [bliːtʃ]
cut:


n. 漂白剂 whitening chemical
example: Bleach can disinfect surfaces but must be used carefully.
example_zh: 漂白剂可以给表面消毒，但必须谨慎使用。
phrase: bleach coral reefs - 使珊瑚礁白化
phrase: bleach recycled paper - 漂白再生纸

blend [blend]
cut:


v. /n. 混合 mix, combine
example: The artist blended blue and green to paint the shallow water.
example_zh: 艺术家混合蓝色和绿色来画浅水。

blip [blɪp]
cut:


n. 雷达上显示的点 small signal spot
example: A small blip appeared on the radar screen.
example_zh: 雷达屏幕上出现了一个小点。

blossom [ˈblɑːsəm]
cut:


1. n. 花 bloom
example: Apple blossom covered the orchard in spring.
example_zh: 春天，苹果花覆盖了果园。

2. v. 开花 bloom
example: The desert blossoms after rare winter rain.
example_zh: 罕见冬雨后，沙漠开花。

blues [bluːz]
cut:


1. n. 抑郁，沮丧 gloom, depressed spirits
example: The long winter gave many residents the blues.
example_zh: 漫长冬季让许多居民感到沮丧。

2. n. 布鲁斯音乐 music
example: Blues music grew from pain, work, and memory.
example_zh: 布鲁斯音乐源于痛苦、劳动和记忆。

bluff [blʌf]
cut:


1. n. 悬崖，绝壁 cliff, deceive
example: The village stood on a bluff above the river.
example_zh: 村庄坐落在河上方的悬崖上。

2. v. 诈骗，吓唬 cliff, deceive
example: The trader tried to bluff buyers with false claims.
example_zh: 商人试图用虚假说法吓唬买家。

blur [blɜːr]
cut:


v. 使…模糊 make indistinct
example: Rain on the window began to blur the view of the street.
example_zh: 窗上的雨水开始模糊街景。

blush [blʌʃ]
cut:


v. 脸红，羞愧 flush
example: She began to blush when the class praised her drawing.
example_zh: 全班称赞她的画时，她开始脸红。

boast [boʊst]
cut:


n. / v. 自我夸耀 brag
example: The brochure boasts that the hotel has the best view of the bay.
example_zh: 小册子夸称这家酒店拥有海湾最佳景观。

bog [bɑːɡ]
cut:


n. 沼泽 swamp
example: A bog stores water and preserves plant remains in wet soil.
example_zh: 沼泽储存水分，并在湿土中保存植物残骸。

bold [boʊld]
cut:
b/old
连接音/年长

adj. 大胆的 daring
example: A bold decision saved the village from repeated flooding.
example_zh: 一个大胆决定使村庄免受反复洪水影响。

bolster [ˈboʊlstər]
cut:


1. n. 垫子，枕垫 support cushion
example: Reducing food imports may bolster local farming if consumers still have enough choice.
example_zh: 如果消费者仍有足够选择，减少食品进口可能支持本地农业。

2. v. 支持 support
example: Extra funding bolstered the hospital during the outbreak.
example_zh: 额外资金在疫情期间支持了医院。

bonanza [bəˈnænzə]
cut:


1. n. 富矿带 rich source, good luck
example: The miners hoped the new vein would become a bonanza.
example_zh: 矿工希望新矿脉会成为富矿带。

2. n. 带来好运的事 rich source, good luck
example: The festival was a bonanza for local restaurants.
example_zh: 这个节日给当地餐馆带来了好运。

bony [ˈboʊni]
cut:


adj. 瘦骨嶙峋的 thin, bone-like
example: The bony fish fossil was preserved in a thin layer of stone.
example_zh: 这块硬骨鱼化石保存在薄薄岩层中。

bookstore [ˈbʊkstɔːr]
cut:


n. 书店 bookshop
example: The bookstore kept a shelf for local history and maps.
example_zh: 书店留了一排书架放地方历史和地图。

boom [buːm]
cut:


1. n. 繁荣 expansion
example: The town enjoyed a boom after the railway opened.
example_zh: 铁路开通后，小镇经历了繁荣。

2. v. 迅速增长 celerity
example: Tourism boomed when the old castle was restored.
example_zh: 旧城堡修复后，旅游业迅速增长。

boon [buːn]
cut:
boon

n. 恩惠，恩赐 blessing, benefit
example: The new well was a boon to farmers during the dry season.
example_zh: 旱季里，新水井给农民带来了恩惠。

boost [buːst]
cut:


v. 提高，推进 raise, push
example: Better lighting can boost safety in the station at night.
example_zh: 更好的照明能提高车站夜间安全。

boulder [ˈboʊldər]
cut:


n. 大石头 stone, rock
example: A fallen boulder blocked the mountain road.
example_zh: 一块落石堵住了山路。

bounce [baʊns]
cut:


v. / n. （使）弹，（使）反弹 spring back
example: The ball bounced off the wall and rolled into the drain.
example_zh: 球从墙上反弹，滚进了排水沟。

bouquet [buˈkeɪ]
cut:


n. 花束 bunch
example: The bouquet on the table made the room feel welcoming.
example_zh: 桌上的花束让房间显得温馨。
phrase: bouquet garni - 香料包

braid [breɪd]
cut:


v. 编织 weave
example: Workers braided thin ropes into a stronger cable.
example_zh: 工人把细绳编成更结实的缆绳。

breathing [ˈbriːðɪ]
cut:


n. 呼吸 respiration
phrase: cell breathing - 细胞呼吸

breed [briːd]
cut:


1. n. 品种 animal kind, produce young
example: This breed of sheep survives well in cold mountains.
example_zh: 这个绵羊品种能在寒冷山区很好生存。

2. v. 饲养 raise
example: The farm breeds horses for long-distance travel.
example_zh: 农场饲养适合长途旅行的马。

3. v. 繁殖 reproduce
example: Mosquitoes breed in standing water.
example_zh: 蚊子在静水中繁殖。

brighten [ˈbraɪtn]
cut:


v. 使快活 make brighter or happier
example: New windows brighten the classroom during winter mornings.
example_zh: 新窗户让冬日早晨的教室更明亮。

brilliance [ˈbrɪliəns]
cut:


1. n. 光辉 radiance
example: The brilliance of the snow made sunglasses necessary.
example_zh: 雪的光辉使太阳镜成为必需。

2. n. 显赫 brightness, excellence
example: Her brilliance in mathematics was noticed early.
example_zh: 她在数学上的显赫才华很早就被注意到。

brilliant [ˈbrɪliənt]
cut:


1. adj. 闪耀的 bright
example: Brilliant stars filled the winter sky.
example_zh: 明亮星星布满冬夜天空。

2. adj. 杰出的 outstanding
example: The engineer offered a brilliant solution to the water problem.
example_zh: 工程师提出了杰出的水问题解决方案。

brochure [broʊˈʃʊr]
cut:


n. 小册子 pamphlet, booklet
example: The brochure explains the museum's opening hours and main exhibits.
example_zh: 小册子说明了博物馆开放时间和主要展品。

bruise [bruːz]
cut:


1. v. 使…受挫伤 skin injury, hurt
example: The fall bruised his shoulder.
example_zh: 跌倒使他的肩膀受挫伤。

2. n. 伤痕，擦痕，青肿 skin injury, hurt
example: A dark bruise appeared on her arm.
example_zh: 她手臂上出现一块青肿。

buck [bʌk]
cut:


n. 美元 male deer, dollar
example: A single buck could buy a meal in the old mining town.
example_zh: 在旧矿镇，一美元可以买一顿饭。

bud [bʌd]
cut:


n. 芽，蓓蕾 young flower shoot
example: A bud opened after three days of warm rain.
example_zh: 三天温暖降雨后，花芽开放了。

buddy [ˈbʌdi]
cut:


n. 密友，伙伴 companion
example: His buddy helped carry water back to the camp.
example_zh: 他的伙伴帮忙把水带回营地。
phrase: buddy system - 各负责另一人之安全的两人同行制

bulk [bʌlk]
cut:


1. n. （大）体积 volume
example: The bulk of the machine made transport difficult.
example_zh: 机器的大体积使运输困难。

2. n. 大部分 majority
example: The bulk of the budget went to roads and schools.
example_zh: 预算的大部分用于道路和学校。

bulletin [ˈbʊlətɪn]
cut:
bullet/in
子弹/进入；向内；否定

1. n. 简明新闻 short notice
example: The radio issued a bulletin about the approaching storm.
example_zh: 广播发布了一条关于逼近风暴的简明新闻。

2. n. 公告 short notice
example: A bulletin on the wall announced the new clinic hours.
example_zh: 墙上的公告宣布了诊所新开放时间。

bump [bʌmp]
cut:


1. v. 撞（破） hit
example: The boat bumped against the pier in the wind.
example_zh: 船在风中撞上码头。

2. n. 肿块 raised swelling, hit
example: A bump on the road shook the cart.
example_zh: 路上的凸块震动了大车。

bunch [bʌntʃ]
cut:


1. n. （一）簇 cluster
example: A bunch of wildflowers stood in a clay pot.
example_zh: 一簇野花插在陶罐里。

2. n. 束，捆 beam
example: He carried a bunch of papers tied with string.
example_zh: 他拿着一捆用绳子系住的文件。

3. n. 串，一串 cluster
example: A bunch of grapes hung near the window.
example_zh: 一串葡萄挂在窗边。

4. n. 一帮，一伙 gang
example: A bunch of teenagers waited outside the cinema.
example_zh: 一伙青少年在电影院外等待。

bureau [ˈbjʊroʊ]
cut:


n. 局，署 office, agency
example: The weather bureau issued a warning before the storm arrived.
example_zh: 气象局在风暴到来前发布了预警。
phrase: census bureau data - 人口普查局数据
phrase: bureau of environmental protection - 环境保护局

burgeon [ˈbɜːrdʒən]
cut:


v. 迅速成长，发展 bloom, flourish
example: Online shopping may burgeon rapidly when delivery services become cheaper and more reliable.
example_zh: 当快递服务更便宜、更可靠时，网购可能快速发展。
phrase: burgeon rapidly - 快速发展
phrase: burgeon into an industry - 发展成产业
phrase: burgeoned market - 发展壮大的市场
phrase: burgeoning industry - 蓬勃发展的产业

bush [bʊʃ]
cut:


n. 矮树丛 shrub
example: A thorny bush grew beside the dry path.
example_zh: 干燥小路旁长着一丛带刺灌木。
phrase: beat about the bush - 旁敲侧击

butter [ˈbʌtər]
cut:


n. 黄油，牛油 fatty dairy spread
example: Butter melts quickly when left near the stove.
example_zh: 黄油放在炉子旁会很快融化。
phrase: butter flavor - 黄油味
phrase: butter production - 黄油生产

by-product [ˈbaɪˌprɑːdʌkt]
cut:


n. 副产品 product
example: An industrial by-product may become valuable if engineers discover a safe way to reuse it.
example_zh: 如果工程师发现安全再利用方式，工业副产品可能变得有价值。
phrase: industrial by-product - 工业副产品
phrase: chemical by-product - 化学副产品

cabin [ˈkæbɪn]
cut:


n. 小屋 hut, cottage
example: The cabin sheltered hikers during the snowstorm.
example_zh: 雪暴期间，小屋为徒步者提供了庇护。

cabinet [ˈkæbɪnət]
cut:


1. n. 内阁 cupboard, government group
example: The cabinet met to discuss the food shortage.
example_zh: 内阁开会讨论食物短缺。

2. n. 贮藏橱 storage
example: Medicine was locked in a cabinet above the sink.
example_zh: 药品锁在水槽上方的贮藏橱里。

3. n. 陈列柜 cupboard, government group
example: The museum kept coins in a glass cabinet.
example_zh: 博物馆把硬币保存在玻璃陈列柜里。

cactus [ˈkæktəs]
cut:


n. cacti] 仙人掌 person
example: A cactus stores water in its thick stem.
example_zh: 仙人掌把水储存在厚茎中。

cafeteria [ˌkæfəˈtɪriə]
cut:


n. 自助餐厅 cafe
example: The cafeteria served simple meals to students after evening classes.
example_zh: 自助餐厅在晚课后给学生提供简单餐食。

calculus [ˈkælkjələs]
cut:
calcul/us
计算/使用

n. 微积分 advanced mathematics
example: Calculus helps engineers describe changing speed and force.
example_zh: 微积分帮助工程师描述变化中的速度和力。
phrase: differential calculus - 微分学
phrase: integral calculus - 积分学
phrase: calculus notation - 微积分记号

campus [ˈkæmpəs]
cut:
camp/us
野营地/我们

n. （大学）校园 university
example: The campus expanded after the university built a new library.
example_zh: 大学建成新图书馆后，校园扩大了。
phrase: live on campus - 住校
phrase: campus safety policy - 校园安全政策

cancel [ˈkænsl]
cut:


1. v. 取消，把…作废 abolish
example: The school cancelled classes because of the storm.
example_zh: 学校因风暴取消课程。

2. v. 删去，删除 ，划掉 call off, cross out
example: The editor cancelled several repeated sentences.
example_zh: 编辑删去了几句重复句子。

3. v. 相互抵消 mutual
example: The two payments cancelled each other out.
example_zh: 两笔付款相互抵消。

cannibalism [ˈkænɪbəlɪzəm]
cut:


n. 嗜食同类 eating one's own species
example: Cannibalism can occur in some species when food is extremely scarce.
example_zh: 食物极度稀缺时，某些物种可能出现同类相食。

canvas [ˈkænvəs]
cut:


1. n. 帆布 sail
example: The sailors repaired the torn canvas before leaving port.
example_zh: 水手离港前修补了破帆布。

2. n. 画布 strong cloth
example: The painter stretched a new canvas over the frame.
example_zh: 画家把新画布绷在框架上。

cape [keɪp]
cut:


n. 海角，岬 angle
example: The lighthouse stands on a cape that reaches into the sea.
example_zh: 灯塔矗立在伸入海中的海角上。

captive [ˈkæptɪv]
cut:
capt/ive
抓/形容词

n. 俘虏，猎物 quarry
phrase: war captive - 战争俘虏

captivity [kæpˈtɪvəti]
cut:
capt/ivity
抓住/表

n. 囚禁，拘留 confinement
example: Animals raised in captivity may struggle to survive in the wild.
example_zh: 圈养长大的动物可能难以在野外生存。

cardiac [ˈkɑːrdiæk]
cut:


1. adj. 心脏的 of or relating to the heart
example: Cardiac muscle works continuously throughout life.
example_zh: 心脏肌肉终生持续工作。

2. adj. 心脏病的 disease
example: The patient entered the cardiac ward after surgery.
example_zh: 病人手术后进入心脏病病房。

cardinal [ˈkɑːrdɪnl]
cut:
card/inal
心脏的/形容词；名词

1. adj. 主要的，最重要的 main, essential
example: The cardinal rule is to keep drinking water clean.
example_zh: 最重要规则是保持饮用水清洁。

2. n. 红衣凤头鸟 main, red bird
example: A red cardinal landed on the fence.
example_zh: 一只红衣凤头鸟落在栅栏上。

coincide [ˌkoʊɪnˈsaɪd]
cut:
co/in/cide
共同/进入；向内；否定/切

example_zh: 房租上涨可能与就业增长同时发生，但工人仍可能受苦。

collaborator [kəˈlæbəreɪtər]
cut:

colonize [ˈkɑːlənaɪz]
cut:

combustible [kəmˈbʌstəbl]
cut:
com/bust/ible
共同；加强/燃烧/能够；形容词

adj. 可燃的，易燃的 flammable

comic [ˈkɑːmɪk]
cut:

example_zh: 滑稽场景能让严肃戏剧更容易观看。

commemorate [kəˈmeməreɪt]
cut:
com/memor/ate
共同/记住/动词；使成为

example_zh: 博物馆可以纪念历史事件，同时帮助游客理解文化身份和民族记忆。

example: The statue commemorates workers who died in the mine.
example_zh: 这座雕像纪念在矿井中死去的工人。

comment [ˈkɑːment]
cut:
com/ment
共同/思考；神智

1. n. /vi. 评论 review

example_zh: 几名读者评论了这张不清楚的图表。

commodity [kəˈmɑːdəti]

com/mod/ity

example_zh: 盐曾是内陆城镇有价值的日用品。

compact [ˈkɑːmpækt]
cut:


1. adj. 紧凑的 small and dense

2. adj. 简洁的 [kəmˈpækt] vt. 压缩 compress

comparative [kəmˈpærətɪv]
cut:

2. adj. 相当的，接近的 proximity

compatible [kəmˈpætəbl]
cut:
com/pat/ible
共同；加强/＝path感情/能够；形容词

competence [ˈkɑːmpɪtəns]
cut:
compete/ence
compet(e)（竞争）/性质；状态；名词

1. n. 胜任 ability, skill
example: Professional competence matters when bridges are inspected.
example_zh: 检查桥梁时，专业胜任很重要。

2. n. 能力 ability
example: Her competence in statistics improved the whole project.
example_zh: 她在统计方面的能力改善了整个项目。

competing [kəmˈpiːtɪ]
cut:


adj. 有竞争力的，不相上下的 rival, contesting

com/pile

example_zh: 政府在判断老龄化人口是否威胁公共服务前，应汇编统计数据。

2. v. 汇编 put together

example_zh: 研究者汇编数据，使零散证据变得可读。

complacence [kəmˈpleɪsns]

example_zh: 自满会让安全系统随着时间变得危险。

complain [kəmˈpleɪn]
cut:
com/plain
加强/平常的

example: Residents complained about noise from the factory.
example_zh: 居民抱怨工厂噪音。

2. v. 申诉 express dissatisfaction
example: Workers complained to the court about unpaid wages.
example_zh: 工人就拖欠工资向法院申诉。

complement [ˈkɑːmplɪmənt]
cut:
com/ple/ment
加强/满，填满/心智；名词

1. v. 补充，使完善 supplement, complete
example: Public transport and cycling can complement each other in a healthy city.
example_zh: 在健康城市中，公共交通和骑行可以相互补充。

2. v. 与…相配 to match
example: The new library complements the nearby school.
example_zh: 新图书馆与附近学校相配。

completion [kəmˈpliːʃn]
cut:


n. 完成，实现 accomplishment, realization
phrase: project completion delay - 项目竣工延迟

complicated [ˈkɑːmplɪkeɪtɪd]
cut:


1. adj. 难懂的 hard to understand, elusive
example: The instructions were too complicated for new users.
example_zh: 这些说明对新用户来说太难懂。

2. adj. 复杂的 complex
example: A complicated legal process delayed the repair work.
example_zh: 复杂法律程序推迟了维修工作。

compliment [ˈkɑːmplɪmənt]
cut:


1. n. 赞美，恭维 praise
example: The teacher gave a compliment on the student's careful drawing.
example_zh: 老师赞美学生细致的画。

2. n. ［常pl.］问候 regards
example: Please give my compliments to the cook.
example_zh: 请向厨师转达我的问候。

comply [kəmˈplaɪ]
cut:
com/ply
共同；加强/重

v. 服从，遵守 conform, submit
example: Factories must comply with rules on waste water.
example_zh: 工厂必须遵守废水规定。
phrase: comply with regulations - 遵守规定
phrase: comply with safety standards - 遵守安全标准

comprehensive [ˌkɑːmprɪˈhensɪv]
cut:


adj. 全面的，综合的 synthesis
phrase: comprehensive reform - 全面改革

concave [kɑːnˈkeɪv]
cut:
con/cave
共同；加强/空；洞

adj. 凹的 curving inward
example: A concave mirror can focus light onto one point.
example_zh: 凹面镜可以把光聚焦到一点。
phrase: concave lens - 凹透镜

concede [kənˈsiːd]
cut:
con/cede
共同；加强/割让

1. v. 承认 grant
example: Officials conceded that the warning had come too late.
example_zh: 官员承认警告来得太晚。

2. v. 让步 yield
example: The company conceded better safety equipment after the strike.
example_zh: 罢工后，公司让步，同意提供更好安全设备。

concise [kənˈsaɪs]
cut:
con/cise
共同；加强/切掉

adj. 简明的，简练的 terse
example: A concise explanation helps voters understand complex policies without reading long reports.
example_zh: 简明解释帮助选民不读长报告也能理解复杂政策。
phrase: concise explanation - 简明解释
phrase: concise summary - 简洁总结
phrase: explain concisely - 简洁解释

conclude [kənˈkluːd]
cut:


1. v. 作出结论 treatise
example: Researchers cannot conclude that online learning works without comparing students' long-term outcomes.
example_zh: 研究者若不比较学生长期结果，就不能得出线上学习有效的结论。

2. v. 使…完毕 complete, end
example: Researchers should not conclude too quickly when evidence is incomplete.
example_zh: 当证据不完整时，研究者不应过快得出结论。

conclusive [kənˈkluːsɪv]
cut:


1. adj. 确定的 definitive
phrase: conclusive evidence - 决定性证据

2. adj. 最后的 decisive, final
phrase: conclusive - 最后的

concomitant [kənˈkaːmɪtənt]
cut:


1. adj. 伴随的 accompanying
example: Rapid growth brought concomitant pressure on housing.
example_zh: 快速增长带来了伴随的住房压力。

2. n. 伴随物 accompanying
example: Noise was a concomitant of building the new road.
example_zh: 噪音是修建新路的伴随物。

condensation [ˌkɑːndenˈseɪʃn]
cut:


n. 浓缩，凝结 the act or process of condensing
phrase: data condensation - 数据压缩

condiment [ˈkɑːndɪmənt]
cut:
condi/ment
隐藏/心智；名词

n. 调味品 dressing, flavoring
example: The cook added a spicy condiment to the plain rice.
example_zh: 厨师给白米饭加了辛辣调味品。

conductor [kənˈdʌktər]
cut:


1. n. 导体 leader, transmitting material
phrase: electrical conductor - 导体

2. n. （乐队等的）指挥 leader, transmitting material
phrase: orchestra conductor - 乐队指挥

conference [ˈkɑːnfərəns]
cut:
con/fer/ence
共同/带来/性质；状态；名词

1. n. 会议 session, meeting
phrase: academic conference - 学术会议

2. n. 讨论会 meeting, consultation
phrase: press conference - 新闻发布会

confine [kənˈfaɪn]
cut:
con/fine
加强/限制

v. 限制 restrict, limit
example: Teachers should confine discussion to evidence when students debate controversial social issues.
example_zh: 当学生讨论有争议的社会问题时，教师应将讨论限于证据。
phrase: confine discussion to evidence - 将讨论限于证据
phrase: confine traffic to main roads - 将交通限制在主路
phrase: confine movement - 限制行动
phrase: confined space - 狭小空间

confused [kənˈfjuːzd]
cut:


adj. 困惑的，不了解的 bewildered
example: Confused passengers waited for a clearer announcement.
example_zh: 困惑的乘客等待更清楚的通知。

confusion [kənˈfjuːʒn]
cut:


n. 混乱，混淆 disorder, uncertainty
phrase: lead to confusion - 导致混乱

congenial [kənˈdʒiːniəl]
cut:
con/geni/al
共同；加强/＝genius才能/形容词；名词

1. adj. 性格温和的 gentle
example: The congenial teacher made nervous students feel safe.
example_zh: 性格温和的老师让紧张学生感到安全。

2. adj. 相宜的 kindred
example: The quiet room was congenial to careful study.
example_zh: 安静房间适宜认真学习。

congratulation [kənˌɡrætʃuˈleɪʃn]
cut:


n. 祝贺，道喜 expression of praise
example: The letter of congratulation arrived after the prize was announced.
example_zh: 获奖公布后，祝贺信到了。

congressional [kənˈɡreʃənl]
cut:


1. adj. 代表大会的，会议的 session, meeting
example: The congressional meeting gathered representatives from every province.
example_zh: 代表大会会议聚集了各省代表。

2. adj. 国会的 parliament-related
example: Congressional leaders debated the budget for weeks.
example_zh: 国会领导人就预算辩论了数周。

3. adj. 最高立法机关的 peak, highest
example: Congressional authority over spending was central to the case.
example_zh: 最高立法机关对支出的权力是案件核心。

consideration [kənˌsɪdəˈreɪʃn]
cut:


1. n. 考虑，思考 think
phrase: ethical consideration in research - 研究中的伦理考虑

2. n. 体谅，照顾 thought, care
phrase: consideration in contract law - 合同法中的对价

3. n. 需要考虑的事 consider
phrase: careful consideration - 仔细考虑

4. n. 理由 thought, care, reason
phrase: critical consideration - 批判性反思

considering [kənˈsɪdərɪ]
cut:


1. prep. 就…而论 treatise
example: Considering the cost, the repair was a sensible choice.
example_zh: 就成本而论，维修是明智选择。

2. prep. 照…说来 taking into account
example: Considering his age, the old sailor walked quickly.
example_zh: 照他的年龄说来，这位老水手走得很快。

3. prep. 鉴于 regarding
example: Considering the storm, the school closed early.
example_zh: 鉴于风暴，学校提前关闭。

consistency [kənˈsɪstənsi]
cut:
consist/ency
一致；组成/名词

1. n. 浓度，密度 density
phrase: logical consistency - 逻辑一致性

2. n. 一致性，协调 quality, property
phrase: policy consistency - 政策一致性

3. n. 连接，结合 connect
phrase: behavioural consistency - 行为规律性

consistent [kənˈsɪstənt]
cut:
con/sis/tent
共同；加强/状态；过程；名词/拉紧

1. adj. 一致的 coherent
phrase: consistent argument - 连贯论证

2. adj. 稳定的 sustained
phrase: consistent values - 相容价值

3. adj. 调和的 reconcile
phrase: consistent pattern - 一致模式

consistently [kənˈsɪstəntli]
cut:
con/sis/tent/ly
共同；加强/状态；过程；名词/拉紧/副词

adv. 一致地 steadily, uniformly
phrase: work consistently - 相容运行

consonant [ˈkɑːnsənənt]
cut:
con/son/ant
共同/声音/形容词；人；物

1. adj. 协调的 harmonious
example: The new rule is consonant with earlier court decisions.
example_zh: 新规则与早期法院判决相协调。

2. n. 辅音 speech sound
example: The word begins with a consonant, not a vowel.
example_zh: 这个词以辅音开头，而不是元音。

consort [kənˈsɔːrt]
cut:
con/sort
共同/类型

v. 结交 associate
example: The trader chose to consort with officials who controlled the port.
example_zh: 商人选择与控制港口的官员结交。

constantly [ˈkɑːnstəntli]
cut:
con/stant/ly
共同；加强/站立；放置/副词

1. adv. 不断地，坚持不懈地 continually
phrase: constantly changing environment - 不断变化的环境

2. adv. 经常地 regularly, always
phrase: constantly monitor emissions - 持续监测排放

constituent [kənˈstʃuənt]
cut:


1. n. 要素，组分 component, element
example: Oxygen is a constituent of water.
example_zh: 氧是水的组成要素。

2. n. 选民 electorate
example: Each constituent wrote to the representative about road repairs.
example_zh: 每位选民都给代表写信谈道路维修。

constricted [kənˈstrɪktɪd]
cut:


1. adj. 狭窄的 confined
example: The constricted passage made it hard to carry equipment.
example_zh: 狭窄通道使搬运设备变得困难。

2. adj. 收缩的 contractive
example: Constricted blood vessels can raise pressure in the body.
example_zh: 收缩的血管会提高体内压力。

contagious [kənˈteɪdʒəs]
cut:
con/tag/ious
共同；加强/接触/形容词

adj. 传染性的，有感染力的 catching
example: A contagious disease can spread before symptoms appear.
example_zh: 传染病可能在症状出现前传播。
phrase: contagious disease - 传染病
phrase: contagious laughter - 有感染力的笑声

contest [ˈkɑːntest]
cut:
con/test
共同/测试，证据

1. n. 竞 game
example: The cooking contest attracted teams from nearby villages.
example_zh: 烹饪竞赛吸引了附近村庄的队伍。

2. n. 辩论 debate
example: The contest over water rights lasted for years.
example_zh: 关于用水权的辩论持续了多年。

continuation [kənˌtɪnjuˈeɪʃn]
cut:


1. n. 延长 extension, ongoing part
example: The continuation of the deadline gave families time to apply.
example_zh: 期限的延长给家庭留下申请时间。

2. n. 延续 prolongation
example: The second volume is a continuation of the same story.
example_zh: 第二卷是同一故事的延续。

continuum [kənˈtɪnjuəm]
cut:


n. 连续统一体 a coherent whole
example: Language ability lies on a continuum rather than in two fixed categories.
example_zh: 语言能力处于连续体上，而不是两个固定类别中。

contradict [ˌkɑːntrəˈdɪkt]
cut:
contra/dict
反/说话，断言

1. v. 反驳 refute
example: Online rumours may contradict official data and confuse patients during public health crises.
example_zh: 在公共卫生危机期间，网络谣言可能与官方数据矛盾并让患者困惑。

2. v. 同…矛盾，同…抵触 shield
example: The new data contradict the minister's earlier statement.
example_zh: 新数据同部长早前声明相矛盾。

controversy [ˈkɑːntrəvɜːrsi]
cut:
contro/vers/y
相反/转/名词；形容词

n. 争论，辩论 dispute, argument
example: A controversy becomes productive when it clarifies the real disagreement.
example_zh: 当争议澄清真正分歧时，它会变得有生产性。
phrase: public controversy - 公共争议
phrase: scientific controversy - 科学争议
phrase: controversy over policy - 政策争议

convenience [kənˈviːniəns]
cut:
con/ven/i/ence
共同/来/i/性质；状态；名词

1. n. 便利 fitness or suitability
example: The convenience of the new bus route helped older residents.
example_zh: 新公交路线的便利帮助了老年居民。

2. n. 便利设施 ease, useful facility
example: The station added conveniences such as toilets and drinking water.
example_zh: 车站增设了厕所和饮用水等便利设施。

converge [kənˈvɜːrdʒ]
cut:
con/verge
共同；加强/转

v. 会聚，聚合 assemble, aggregate
example: Different transport policies may converge on a solution that reduces car dependence.
example_zh: 不同交通政策可能汇聚成一个减少汽车依赖的解决方案。
phrase: converge on a solution - 汇聚到解决方案
phrase: converge in cities - 汇聚到城市
phrase: converge on a point - 汇聚到一点
phrase: ideas converge - 观点趋同

conversion [kənˈvɜːrʒn]
cut:
con/vers/ion
共同；加强/转/动作；状态；名词

1. n. 转变 convert
example: The conversion of the warehouse into housing took two years.
example_zh: 把仓库转变为住房花了两年。

2. n. 改变信仰 change
example: His conversion changed the way his family observed festivals.
example_zh: 他的改变信仰改变了家人过节的方式。

convex [ˈkɑːnveks]
cut:


adj. 凸出的 bulging
example: A convex lens bends light toward a focus.
example_zh: 凸透镜会把光线折向焦点。
phrase: convex lens - 凸透镜

convey [kənˈveɪ]
cut:
con/vey
共同/道路

1. v. 运（送、输） carry, transport
example: News reports should convey public concern without exaggerating crime or creating panic.
example_zh: 新闻报道应传达公众担忧，而不是夸大犯罪或制造恐慌。

2. v. 传达 communicate, transfer
example: Images can convey emotion before viewers understand the facts.
example_zh: 图像可以在观众理解事实之前先传达情感。

convince [kənˈvɪns]
cut:
con/vince
全部/征服，克服

v. 使确信，说服 persuade, assure
example: The data convinced the committee to change its plan.
example_zh: 数据说服委员会改变计划。
phrase: convince voters - 说服选民

cookout [ˈkʊkaʊt]
cut:


1. n. 野外郊游时烹调的野餐，野烹食物 outdoor meal
example: The school held a cookout beside the lake.
example_zh: 学校在湖边举行野外烹调野餐。

2. adj. 野外烹饮聚会的 outdoor meal
example: Cookout meals were served after the community games.
example_zh: 社区比赛后供应野外烹饮聚会餐食。

cooperative [koʊˈɑːpərətɪv]
cut:


adj. 合作的，协力的 cooperation
phrase: cooperative governance model - 合作治理模式

copier [ˈkɑːpiər]
cut:


1. n. 影印机 copying machine
example: The office copier broke before the meeting papers were ready.
example_zh: 会议材料准备好前，办公室影印机坏了。

2. n. 复印机 copying machine
example: A copier in the library lets students duplicate old articles.
example_zh: 图书馆的复印机让学生复印旧文章。

copious [ˈkoʊpiəs]
cut:


adj. 丰富的，富饶的 abundance
example: Copious rainfall filled the reservoir within a week.
example_zh: 充沛降雨在一周内填满了水库。

copper [ˈkɑːpər]
cut:
cop/per
警察/贯穿；完全

n. 铜（币） reddish metal
example: Copper wires carry electricity through the building.
example_zh: 铜线把电传遍建筑物。

cornerstone [ˈkɔːrnərstoʊn]
cut:


1. n. 墙角石，奠基石 angle
example: The cornerstone of the school was laid in 1912.
example_zh: 这所学校的奠基石于 1912 年铺设。

2. n. 柱石 stone, rock
example: Trust is a cornerstone of medical care.
example_zh: 信任是医疗护理的柱石。

3. n. 基础 foundation
example: Reading is the cornerstone of later learning.
example_zh: 阅读是后续学习的基础。

corona [kəˈroʊnə]
cut:


n. 日冕 ，光环 aura
example: The corona becomes visible during a total solar eclipse.
example_zh: 日全食期间，日冕会变得可见。

corps [kɔːr]
cut:
corp/s
团体/连接音

n. 军团，兵团 military body
example: The medical corps set up tents near the damaged bridge.
example_zh: 医疗队在受损桥梁附近搭起帐篷。
phrase: diplomatic corps - 外交使团
phrase: medical corps in wartime - 战时医疗队

costume [ˈkɑːstuːm]
cut:


1. n. 服饰 dress
example: The actors wore traditional costumes during the festival play.
example_zh: 演员在节日戏剧中穿传统服饰。

2. v. 装束 beam
example: The designer costumed the dancers in blue and silver.
example_zh: 设计师给舞者装束成蓝银色。

counseling [ˈkaʊnsəlɪ]
cut:


n. 咨询服务 professional guidance of the individual
example: Counseling helped students manage stress before exams.
example_zh: 咨询服务帮助学生管理考前压力。

counselor [ˈkaʊnsələr]
cut:


n. 顾问，法律顾问 advisor
example: A counselor listened before suggesting practical steps.
example_zh: 顾问先倾听，然后提出实际步骤。

counter [ˈkaʊntər]
cut:


1. n. 柜台 station, platform
example: Medicine was kept behind the pharmacy counter.
example_zh: 药品放在药房柜台后面。

2. n. 计数器 counting device, opposite
example: The counter recorded every visitor entering the museum.
example_zh: 计数器记录每位进入博物馆的访客。

3. adv. /a. 相反（的） counting device, opposite
example: The evidence runs counter to the official explanation.
example_zh: 证据与官方解释相反。

4. v. 反对，反击 opposition, objection
example: The lawyer countered the accusation with new documents.
example_zh: 律师用新文件反击指控。

counteract [ˌkaʊntərˈækt]
cut:
counter/act
反/动作

v. 消除 ，抵消 neutralize
phrase: counteract inflationary pressure - 抵消通胀压力

couple [ˈkʌpl]
cut:


1. n. （一）对，（一）双 pair
example: A couple of lamps lit the narrow street.
example_zh: 几盏灯照亮了狭窄街道。

2. n. 夫妇 pair, married pair
example: The elderly couple ran a small bookshop.
example_zh: 这对老夫妇经营一家小书店。

3. n. ［物］力偶，电偶 pair, married pair
example: The physicist explained how a force couple turns a body.
example_zh: 物理学家解释力偶如何使物体转动。

4. v. 连接，结合 connect
example: The bridge couples the old town with the new district.
example_zh: 这座桥连接旧城和新区。

coupon [ˈkuːpɑːn]
cut:


n. 礼券，优惠券 gift certificate
example: The coupon reduced the price of the medicine.
example_zh: 优惠券降低了药品价格。

courageous [kəˈreɪdʒəs]
cut:
courage/ous
勇气/…的

adj. 勇敢的，有胆量的 brave
phrase: courageous whistleblower testimony - 勇敢举报者证词

courier [ˈkʊriər]
cut:


n. 送急件的人，信使 messenger
example: A courier delivered the documents before the hearing began.
example_zh: 信使在听证会开始前送达文件。
phrase: courier network efficiency - 快递网络效率

cowhand [ˈkaʊhænd]
cut:


1. n. 牛仔 cattle worker
example: The cowhand repaired fences before moving the cattle.
example_zh: 牛仔在赶牛前修好栅栏。

2. n. 牧牛工 cattle worker
example: A young cowhand worked on the ranch during summer.
example_zh: 一名年轻牧牛工夏天在牧场工作。

crab [kræb]
cut:


n. 蟹 sideways-moving shellfish
example: A crab hides under rocks when the tide goes out.
example_zh: 退潮时，螃蟹躲在岩石下。

cramped [ˈkræmpt]
cut:


adj. （指空间）狭小的，狭窄的 limited
example: Cramped housing made disease spread more easily.
example_zh: 狭小住房使疾病更容易传播。

crazy [ˈkreɪzi]
cut:


adj. 疯狂的，狂热的 insane, deranged
example: The idea sounded crazy until the first test succeeded.
example_zh: 这个想法听起来疯狂，直到第一次测试成功。

creativity [ˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti]
cut:


n. 创造（力） creation

crest [krest]
cut:
c/rest
连接音/休息

n. 顶部 peak

crevice [ˈkrevɪs]

crev/ice
裂开/名词

cut:

crisscross [ˈkrɪskrɔːs]
cut:

phrase: crisscross pattern - 交叉图案
phrase: roads crisscross - 道路纵横交错
phrase: border crossing - 边境通道

criticize [ˈkrɪtɪsaɪz]
cut:


v. 批评，吹毛求疵，非难 find fault, judge
example: Citizens can criticize a policy without rejecting the whole government.
example_zh: 市民可以批评一项政策，而不必否定整个政府。

phrase: criticize government inaction - 批评政府不作为

critique [krɪˈtiːk]
cut:


n. 批评，评论 criticism, comment
example: The critique praised the method but questioned the small sample.
example_zh: 评论赞扬了方法，但质疑样本太小。
phrase: film critique - 影评
phrase: critique of modernization theory - 现代化理论批评
phrase: feminist critique of law - 女性主义法律批评

crooked [ˈkrʊkɪd]
cut:

2. adj. 欺诈的 fraud
example: The crooked deal left farmers with worthless land.
example_zh: 欺诈交易让农民拿到毫无价值的土地。

crossing [ˈkrɔːsɪ]
cut:

example_zh: 货运列车接近时，铁路交叉口会关闭。
phrase: a river crossing - 河流交叉口

crow [kroʊ]
cut:

example_zh: 乌鸦把坚果丢到路上以敲碎外壳。

crude [kruːd]
cut:
c/rud/e
连接音/天然的，粗糙的/e

1. adj. 天然的，未提炼的 unrefined
example: Crude oil must be refined before many uses.
example_zh: 天然原油在许多用途前必须提炼。

2. adj. 粗糙的 rough
example: The shelter was crude but strong enough for winter.
example_zh: 庇护所很粗糙，但足以过冬。

crumple [ˈkrʌmpl]
cut:


1. v. 把…弄皱 wrinkle, collapse
example: She crumpled the letter and threw it into the fire.
example_zh: 她把信弄皱并扔进火里。

2. v. 起皱 rumple

example_zh: 薄金属在重轮下起皱变形。

crusade [kruːˈseɪd]
cut:


1. n. 十字军（远征） expedition

example_zh: 历史课学习了第一次十字军远征。

2. n. 运动 movement

crush [krʌʃ]

example_zh: 威权国家可能在反对派组织起来之前将其镇压。

2. v. 使变皱 press, defeat

example_zh: 孩子一只手把纸杯捏皱了。

cube [kjuːb]
cut:

example_zh: 每块冰块在阳光下几分钟内就融化了。

cue [kjuː]
cut:

example_zh: 老师用图片作为记忆提示。

cultivated [ˈkʌltɪveɪtɪd]
cut:

example_zh: 栽植水稻在水田中长得最好。

2. adj. 有修养的 educated
example: Her cultivated speech impressed the visitors.
example_zh: 她有修养的谈吐给访客留下印象。

curious [ˈkjuriəs]

example_zh: 好奇孩子询问月亮为何改变形状。

example_zh: 求知学生会核查每个说法的来源。

curl [kɜːrl]
cut:

example_zh: 烟在炊火上方卷曲。

cushion [ˈkʊʃn]

example_zh: 垫子让木椅更舒服。

example_zh: 储蓄缓冲了突发疾病对家庭的冲击。

cut:

dairy [ˈderi]
cut:

daisy [ˈdeɪzi]
cut:

dead/line

dealer [ˈdiːlər]

deal/er
交易；处理/人

装饰/动词；使成为

example_zh: 这位护士致力于农村医疗事业。

example_zh: 书中的题献词感谢了作者父母。

3. n. （教堂等的）启用典礼 opening ceremony

example_zh: 教堂启用典礼吸引了各山谷的村民。

de/fect
变坏/做

definitive [dɪˈfɪnətɪv]
cut:

cut:
de/hydr/ate
去掉/水/使

delectable [dɪˈlektəbl]
cut:
d/elect/able
连接音/选/能够；形容词

1. adj. 美味的 delicious

example_zh: 市场出售用当地蜂蜜制作的美味蛋糕。

de/pred/ation

describe [dɪˈskraɪb]

加强/写

1. v. 描写，描述 portray, depict

example_zh: 证人在船沉没前描述了它。

2. v. 称作 call
example: The teacher described the result as unexpected but useful.

cut:


1. adj. 荒废的 obsolete

example_zh: 荒废工厂立在铁路旁。

2. adj. 无人的 void

deserve [dɪˈzɜːrv]
cut:
de/serve
向下；离开/服务

example: Volunteers deserve credit for keeping the clinic open.
example_zh: 志愿者因维持诊所开放而应得荣誉。

2. v. 值得 be entitled to
example: The fragile wetland deserves stronger protection.
example_zh: 这片脆弱湿地值得更强保护。

desire [dɪˈzaɪər]
cut:


1. v. 想要，渴望 long for
example: Many students desire a job that feels meaningful.
example_zh: 许多学生渴望一份有意义的工作。

2. n. 愿望，欲望 appetite
example: A desire for security shaped the family's choices.
example_zh: 对安全的愿望塑造了这个家庭的选择。

desolate [ˈdesələt]
cut:
de/sol/ate
向下；离开/孤独/动词；使成为

adj. 荒凉的 deserted

example_zh: 如果交通连接带来工作和公共服务，荒凉村庄可以恢复。
phrase: desolate village - 荒凉村庄
phrase: desolate landscape - 荒凉景观
phrase: desolated village - 荒废村庄
phrase: stand desolately - 荒凉地矗立

desperate [ˈdespərət]
cut:
de/sper/ate
去掉/希望/动词；使成为

adj. 令人绝望的 despairing

example_zh: 洪水后，绝望的家庭在诊所外等待。

despoil [dɪˈspɔɪl]
cut:
de/spoil
加强/损坏

example_zh: 监管不善的炼油厂如果未经处理就排放废物和烟气，会破坏附近土地。
phrase: despoil sb. of rights - 剥夺某人的权利
phrase: despoil forests - 破坏森林
phrase: despoil landscapes - 破坏景观
phrase: despoil the land - 破坏土地

dessert [dɪˈzɜːrt]
cut:


n. （餐后）甜点 sweet final course
example: The restaurant served fruit as a light dessert.
example_zh: 餐馆用水果作为清淡甜点。

destined [ˈdestɪnd]
cut:


adj. 注定的 doomed
example: The old bridge was destined for demolition after the new road opened.
example_zh: 新路开通后，旧桥注定要被拆除。

destruction [dɪˈstrʌkʃn]
cut:
de/struct/ion
向下；破坏/建立；结构/名词

n. 毁坏，毁灭 destroy
phrase: environmental destruction - 环境破坏

detectable [dɪˈtektəbl]
cut:
detect/able
发现；察觉/能够；形容词

1. adj. 可发觉的 able to be found

2. adj. 可看穿的 apparent

detective [dɪˈtektɪv]
cut:


n. 侦探 investigator
phrase: detective story - 侦探小说

deter [dɪˈtɜːr]
cut:
de/ter
向下；离开/＝terr吓唬

v. 阻止 prevent
example: Bright lights can deter theft around the station.
example_zh: 明亮灯光可以阻止车站周围的盗窃。
phrase: deter crime - 阻止犯罪
phrase: deterring effect - 威慑效果
phrase: deter participation - 阻止参与

detergent [dɪˈtɜːrdʒənt]
cut:
de/terg/ent
向下；离开/擦/形容词；人；物

example_zh: 洗涤剂过量会在洗涤后污染水体。

detest [dɪˈtest]
cut:
de/test
向下；离开/测试

example: Citizens may detest corruption when public money is wasted on empty stadiums.
example_zh: 当公共资金被浪费在空置体育场上时，市民可能憎恶腐败。
phrase: detest corruption - 厌恶腐败
phrase: detest unfair treatment - 厌恶不公平待遇
phrase: detested practice - 被厌恶的做法
phrase: detest injustice - 厌恶不公

devastate [ˈdevəsteɪt]
cut:
de/vast/ate
变坏/大量/动词；使成为

v. 破坏 ruin
example: A single storm can devastate crops near the coast.
example_zh: 一场风暴就能摧毁沿海作物。
phrase: devastate a population - 严重破坏种群

devotion [dɪˈvoʊʃn]
cut:

example: Her devotion to music began in childhood.
example_zh: 她对音乐的热爱始于童年。

2. n. 投入 passion
example: The project required devotion from every volunteer.
example_zh: 这个项目需要每位志愿者投入。

3. n. 献身，奉献 dedication
example: The doctor's devotion to public service impressed the town.
example_zh: 医生对公共服务的献身让小镇印象深刻。

diagnose [ˌdaɪəɡˈnoʊs]
cut:
dia/gnos/e
穿过/知道/e

v. 诊断 identify illness or problem

example_zh: 医生通过比较症状和检测结果诊断疾病。
phrase: diagnose disease - 诊断疾病

diagonal [daɪˈæɡənl]
cut:
dia/gon/al
相对/角/形容词；名词

example_zh: 一条倾斜小路穿过方形花园。

diameter [daɪˈæmɪtər]
cut:
dia/meter
对面/计量，测量

example_zh: 管道直径决定了能通过多少水。

dictate [ˈdɪkteɪt]
cut:
dict/ate
讲话，命令/动词；使成为

1. v. 规定 regulate
example: Safety rules dictate how chemicals must be stored.
example_zh: 安全规则规定化学品必须如何储存。

2. v. 决定 determine
example: Weather will dictate when the rescue flight can leave.
example_zh: 天气将决定救援航班何时能起飞。

diction [ˈdɪkʃn]
cut:
dict/ion
说话/动作；状态；名词

n. 措辞，用语 expression

example_zh: 演讲者的措辞使法律论证更容易理解。

differentiate [ˌdɪfəˈrenʃieɪt]
cut:


1. v. （使）不同 different

2. v. 区别 distinguish

diffuse [dɪˈfjuːz]
cut:
dif/fuse
不同/流

2. v. 扩散 spread
example: Smoke diffused through the open hall.

digression [daɪˈɡreʃn]
cut:

example_zh: 这一章包含一段关于地方节日的题外话。

cut:
di/late
二；分开/放

dilute [daɪˈluːt]
cut:
di/lute
二；分开/冲洗

v. 稀释，淡化 desalt
example: Workers dilute the chemical before using it near plants.
example_zh: 工人在植物附近使用该化学品前会先稀释。

dim [dɪm]
cut:

example_zh: 雾中出现模糊山影。

example: A dim lamp burned in the corner of the room.
example_zh: 房间角落里亮着一盏暗淡灯。

diplomatic [ˈdɪpləˈmætɪk]
cut:


1. adj. 外交的，从事外交的 foreign-relations related

2. adj. 策略的 ，有手腕的 foreign-relations related, tactful

directory [dəˈrektəri]
cut:
direct/ory
指引/物

example_zh: 人名地址录列出了该区每家商店。

2. n. 目录 list
example: The computer directory stored the project files.
example_zh: 电脑目录存放项目文件。

disadvantage [ˌdɪsədˈvæntɪdʒ]
cut:
dis/advantage
不/优点

1. n. 缺点 drawback
example: The main disadvantage of the plan is its high cost.
example_zh: 该计划的主要缺点是成本高。

2. n. 不利 handicap
example: Distance put rural students at a disadvantage.
example_zh: 距离使农村学生处于不利地位。

disappoint [ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪnt]
cut:
dis/appoint
不/任命

example_zh: 歉收使期待恢复的农民失望。

2. v. 使扫兴 fail to satisfy
example: The cancelled concert disappointed the children.
example_zh: 取消的音乐会使孩子们扫兴。

discern [dɪˈsɜːrn]
cut:
dis/cern
分开/区别

example_zh: 当网站在没有证据的情况下提供医疗建议时，读者必须识别隐藏风险。

example: Experts discerned a pattern in the damaged stones.
example_zh: 专家识别出受损石头中的一种模式。

discharge [ˈdɪstʃɑːrdʒ]
cut:
dis/charge
离开/充电

1. n. 流出物 shed
example: Industrial discharge polluted the lower river.
example_zh: 工业流出物污染了下游河段。

2. n. 放电 [dɪsˈtʃɑrdʒ] v. 释放 release

example_zh: 风暴在山上方产生放电。

disciple [dɪˈsaɪpl]
cut:


n. 门徒，弟子 follower, adherent
example: The disciple copied his teacher's methods before developing his own.
example_zh: 弟子先模仿老师的方法，再发展自己的方法。
phrase: religious disciple - 宗教弟子
phrase: disciple of a theory - 理论追随者

discount [ˈdɪskaʊnt]
cut:
dis/count
分离/计算

example_zh: 节日后，商店给工具打折。
phrase: at a discount - 打折扣

disguise [dɪsˈɡaɪz]
cut:
dis/guise
分开；否定/姿态，伪装

1. v. / n. 掩饰 mask

example_zh: 报告用技术语言掩饰薄弱证据。

dis/gust
不/风味

example_zh: 受污染水的气味让访客厌恶。

2. v. 嫌恶 detest, loathe

example_zh: 残忍对待动物使村民嫌恶。

dismal [ˈdɪzməl]
cut:

example_zh: 阴沉云层整个下午覆盖海岸。

2. adj. 忧郁的 blue
example: The team's dismal results discouraged supporters.
example_zh: 团队忧郁糟糕的结果让支持者泄气。

dismay [dɪsˈmeɪ]
cut:
dis/may
不/可能

example_zh: 测试失败让工程师们沮丧。

disorder [dɪsˈɔːrdər]
cut:
dis/order
不/顺序

example_zh: 混乱交通每天都会让大城市对行人而言压力大且不安全。

example_zh: 睡眠失调使集中注意变得困难。

dispersal [dɪˈspɜːsl]
cut:

displacement [dɪsˈpleɪsmənt]
cut:


n. 移置，转移 moving from place

disposal [dɪˈspoʊzl]
cut:

2. n. 处置 get rid of
example: The safe disposal of chemicals requires trained workers.
example_zh: 化学品安全处置需要受训工人。

dispose [dɪˈspoʊz]
cut:

example: Residents may be disposed to cooperate when officials disclose costs honestly and early.
example_zh: 当官员早早诚实披露成本时，居民可能愿意合作。

2. v. 除掉 get rid of

example_zh: 城市在复制旧记录后除掉了它们。

disrepute [ˌdɪsrɪˈpjuːt]
cut:
dis/repute
否定/名声

example_zh: 虚假报告使实验室名誉受损。

disseminate [dɪˈsemɪneɪt]
cut:
dis/semin/ate
分开/种子/动词；使成为

v. 散布，传播 spread
example: Public institutions should disseminate information quickly during health emergencies and natural disasters.
example_zh: 公共机构应在健康紧急事件和自然灾害期间快速传播信息。
phrase: disseminate information - 传播信息
phrase: disseminate research findings - 传播研究发现
phrase: disseminated message - 被传播信息

distasteful [dɪsˈteɪstfl]
cut:


1. adj. （令人）不愉快的 displeasing
example: The joke was distasteful during a serious ceremony.
example_zh: 严肃仪式中这个笑话令人不愉快。

2. adj. 讨厌的 disagreeable
example: Many residents found the advertisement distasteful.
example_zh: 许多居民觉得这则广告讨厌。

distinctive [dɪˈstɪ ktɪv]
cut:
distinct/ive
不同；明显/形容词

1. adj. 出众的 clearly different

2. adj. 有特色的 unique
phrase: distinctive feature - 独特特征

distort [dɪˈstɔːrt]
cut:
dis/tort
坏/扭曲

example_zh: 煽动性标题会扭曲关于犯罪、移民和公共支出的公共讨论。

example: A biased sample can distort the survey results.

distract [dɪˈstrækt]
cut:
dis/tract
分开/拉

example_zh: 街上的噪声会在考试时分散学生注意力。
phrase: distract students - 使学生分心

distress [dɪˈstres]
cut:

example: The injured animal showed clear signs of distress.
example_zh: 受伤动物表现出明显痛苦迹象。
phrase: financial distress indicator - 财务困境指标
phrase: psychological distress after disaster - 灾后心理痛苦

disturb [dɪˈstɜːrb]
cut:
dis/turb
分开/搅动

v. 打扰，扰乱 upset, bother
example: Construction work can disturb birds during nesting season.
example_zh: 施工会在筑巢季干扰鸟类。

phrase: disturb ecological balance - 扰乱生态平衡
phrase: disturb public order - 扰乱公共秩序

disturbance [dɪˈstɜːrbəns]
cut:
dis/turb/ance
分开；否定/扰乱/性质；状态；名词

1. n. 干扰 interference
phrase: supply disturbance - 供应中断

2. n. 骚动 stir
phrase: signal disturbance - 信号干扰

diverse [daɪˈvɜːrs]
cut:
di/vers/e
离开/转/e

1. adj. 不同的 different
example: Diverse perspectives can improve judgement when disagreement is handled honestly.
example_zh: 当分歧被诚实处理时，多样视角可以改善判断。

2. adj. 多样的 varied, various
example: The city attracts people from diverse backgrounds.
example_zh: 这座城市吸引来自多样背景的人。

diversion [daɪˈvɜːrʒn]
cut:
di/vers/ion
离开/转/动作；状态；名词

1. n. 消遣，娱乐 recreation, entertainment
phrase: created a diversion - 分散注意力，声东击西

2. n. 转移，转换 transform
phrase: attention diversion - 注意力转移

documentary [ˌdɑːkjuˈmentri]
cut:


1. adj. 文献的 literature
phrase: documentary evidence in court - 法庭书面证据

2. adj. 纪实的 realistic
phrase: documentary film archive - 纪录片档案

3. n. 纪录片 factual film
phrase: documentary evidence - 书面证据

dogged [ˈdɔːɡɪd]
cut:


1. adj. 顽强的 stubbornly determined
example: Dogged effort kept the rescue work going through the night.
example_zh: 顽强努力让救援工作持续整夜。

2. adj. 顽固的 persevering
example: The dogged investigator refused to abandon the case.
example_zh: 这位顽固坚持的调查员拒绝放弃案件。

domain [doʊˈmeɪn]
cut:

2. n. 领土 territory

example_zh: 河流标记了国王领土的边界。

donate [ˈdoʊneɪt]
cut:
don/ate
给予/动词；使成为

1. v. 捐赠 contribute
example: Families donated blankets after the storm.
example_zh: 风暴后，家庭捐赠了毯子。

2. v. 赠送 present
example: The artist donated a painting to the school.
example_zh: 艺术家把一幅画赠送给学校。

donation [doʊˈneɪʃn]
cut:
don/ation
给予/动作；过程；名词

n. 捐赠，捐款 endowment
example: A small donation helped the clinic buy clean bandages.
example_zh: 一笔小捐款帮助诊所购买干净绷带。
phrase: blood donation - 献血

dormancy [ˈdɔːrmənsi]
cut:
dorm/ancy
睡眠/名词；形容词

1. n. 休眠 inactive state

2. n. 眠状态 condition

3. n. 隐匿 inactive state, hidden state

dormant [ˈdɔːrmənt]
cut:
dorm/ant
睡眠/形容词；人；物

1. adj. 静止的 inactive

example_zh: 如果个人数据仍被保存，休眠账户仍可能造成隐私风险。
